hourlyBriefing.title: 本小时全球动态简报
hourlyBriefing.lead: 根据最新监测信源，本小时重点聚焦驻伊拉克美军撤出进程、迪拜航空客机迫降事件排查，以及南非针对女性暴力引发的社会强烈抗议。
keySignals: 根据巴格达与华盛顿达成的协议，驻伊拉克美军最后一批部队定于周三撤离，伊拉克军队正式接管剩余基地以强化主权与军事能力。
一架 FlyDubai 客机在沙特阿拉伯紧急迫降，此前有关劫机的初步传闻在飞机着陆后已被正式排除。
南非约翰内斯堡附近发生12名女性遇害事件，引发社会对针对女性暴力严重程度的强烈抗议。

dailyBriefing.title: 国际安全动态与突发事件简报
dailyBriefing.lead: 近期国际安全与社会事件呈现多重发展态势：美军根据美伊协议从伊拉克完成撤军并将防务移交伊军；迪拜航空一架客机因紧急情况在沙特迫降并排除了劫机嫌疑；南非多起女性被害案引发公众对暴力犯罪规模的抗议。

themes.name: 驻伊美军撤离与伊拉克主权交接
themes.analysis: 根据巴格达与华盛顿达成的协议，参与打击“伊斯兰国”国际联盟的最后一批美军定于周三撤出伊拉克。伊拉克军方正式接管联盟留下的防空与军事基地，伊拉克政府正寻求加强自身军事能力并重申国家主权；长期生活在美军基地周边、饱受战火波及的当地民众则期盼局势恢复正常。

topStories.title: 印度增加中东原油进口并削减自俄采购量
topStories.originalTitle: India Boosts Middle East Oil Imports, Cuts Russian Flows
topStories.snippet: India has ramped up its crude oil imports from the Middle East while reducing purchases of Russian crude, Indian media have reported, citing data from Kpler. The country, however, is not planning to completely suspend Russian oil imports despite the U.S. threat of 100% tariffs. Oil imports from Middle Eastern producers averaged 3 million barrels daily this month, Kpler said, as quoted by The Telegraph, while Russian oil purchases stood at a daily average of 1.75 million barrels. The Middle East
topStories.fullContent: India has ramped up its crude oil imports from the Middle East while reducing purchases of Russian crude, Indian media have reported, citing data from Kpler. The country, however, is not planning to completely suspend Russian oil imports despite the U.S. threat of 100% tariffs. Oil imports from Middle Eastern producers averaged 3 million barrels daily this month, Kpler said, as quoted by The Telegraph, while Russian oil purchases stood at a daily average of 1.75 million barrels.  The Middle East September average represents a return to pre-war import levels, while the Russian import daily average is a decline from August, when flows averaged 2.1 million barrels daily, per earlier Kpler data that forecast the September average for Russian crude imports at 1.9 million barrels. The decline, however, does not mean Indian refiners are about to stop buying any Russian crude. In fact, Russia remains the biggest single supplier of crude oil to India, even at its smaller September share of the total. That total, by the way, stood at 5.3 million barrels daily, which was an increase of 600,000 barrels daily from August, and an even bigger increase, of 700,000 barrels daily, from a year earlier. “Russia remains a central part of India’s crude import basket, and we do not see the latest decline as India moving away from Russian barrels altogether,” Kpler analyst Sumit Ritolia. India is the second-largest importer of Russian crude oil, behind China, while imports from Russia have accounted for nearly half of all Indian crude purchases in recent months. As one of the biggest buyers of Russian crude oil, India could face tariffs of up to 100% on its goods exported to the United States following the latest sanction package. Moreover, the potential tariffs could sour trade relations just as New Delhi and Washington have been negotiating a bilateral trade deal for month. By Irina Slav for Oilprice.com
topStories.fullTranslation:
据印度媒体援引大宗商品数据分析机构Kpler的数据报道，印度已增加从中东的原油进口，同时减少了对俄罗斯原油的采购。然而，尽管美国发出了征收100%关税的威胁，印度仍不打算完全暂停进口俄罗斯石油。

英国《每日电讯报》（The Telegraph）援引Kpler的数据称，本月印度从中东产油国进口的石油平均达到每日300万桶，而对俄罗斯石油的采购量则维持在每日平均175万桶。中东地区9月份的平均进口水平意味着其已回升至俄乌冲突爆发前的进口水平；而俄罗斯原油的日均进口量则较8月份有所下滑——早前Kpler的数据显示8月份自俄进口量平均为每日210万桶，并曾预测9月份自俄原油进口日均值为190万桶。

然而，这一降幅并不意味着印度炼油商将彻底停止采购俄罗斯原油。事实上，即便9月份在印度总进口量中的占比有所收窄，俄罗斯依然是印度最大的单一原油供应国。顺便提一下，印度当月的原油总进口量达到每日530万桶，较8月份每日增加了60万桶，与去年同期相比更是每日增加了70万桶，增幅更大。

Kpler分析师苏米特·里托利亚（Sumit Ritolia）表示：“俄罗斯仍是印度原油进口篮子的核心组成部分，我们并不认为近期的下滑意味着印度将彻底摆脱对俄罗斯原油的依赖。”

印度是仅次于中国的俄罗斯原油第二大进口国，而近几个月来自俄罗斯的进口量已占到印度原油采购总量的近一半。作为俄罗斯原油的最大买家之一，随着最新制裁方案的出台，印度出口至美国的商品可能面临最高达100%的关税。此外，就在新德里与华盛顿数月来一直在就双边贸易协议进行谈判之际，潜在的关税可能会使双边贸易关系恶化。

作者：伊琳娜·斯拉夫（Irina Slav），为Oilprice.com撰稿

topStories.title: 在旁观多年后，Apple Pay 终于在印度上线
topStories.originalTitle: Apple Pay finally launches in India after years on the sidelines
topStories.snippet: Some of India's largest banks are holding off on supporting Apple Pay initially.
topStories.fullContent:
Apple began rolling out Apple Pay in India on Tuesday, as TechCrunch was first to report. Its first banking partner is Axis Bank, the country’s third-largest private-sector lender. The move brings the company’s payments service to the world’s most populous country after years of delays in a market dominated by the state-backed United Payments Interface (UPI).

The initial rollout is limited. Apple Pay supports eligible Axis Bank cards on Visa and Mastercard, but not India’s homegrown RuPay network. Acceptance will also be restricted to merchants and payment terminals that have been enabled for the service.

Apple said the service would be accepted by “millions of merchants” across India, including Blinkit, Croma, Ixigo, Reliance brands, Tata 1mg, and Zomato. The company has worked with payment service providers including Cashfree, JusPay, Mswipe, Paytm, PayU, Pine Labs, Razorpay, and Worldline to enable Apple Pay acceptance.

Unlike India’s ubiquitous Unified Payments Interface (UPI) system, which lets consumers make instant bank-to-bank payments without relying on cards, Apple Pay is card-based and requires individual issuers and payment infrastructure providers to integrate with the service. This makes a broad rollout more complex. Apple’s commercial terms have also emerged as a sticking point with some of India’s largest banks, the people said.

Apple is seeking a fee of about 20 basis points (0.2%) on transactions, according to the people, a significant bite out of the roughly 40 to 50 basis points (0.4% to 0.5%) of margin in the payments layer. The fee structure is broadly consistent with Apple Pay’s commercial model in other markets, the people said. HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, and SBI Card are not supporting Apple Pay at launch as negotiations over commercial terms continue, one of the people told TechCrunch.

Apple, Axis Bank, HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, and SBI Card did not respond to requests for comment on the launch. Earlier this month, Reuters reported that Apple was preparing to launch Apple Pay in India in October, starting with Axis Bank credit cards.

Apple Pay has entered a payments market that looks markedly different from the U.S. and other card-heavy economies. India’s digital payments boom has been driven largely by UPI, the state-backed system that lets consumers move money directly between bank accounts.

UPI handles the bulk of digital payments in India, where scanning a QR code to pay directly from a bank account has become commonplace. Apple Pay, by contrast, initially addresses a much smaller card payments market.

Nevertheless, Apple Pay could appeal to India’s growing base of iPhone users, who tend to be more affluent and are more likely to use premium credit cards. Those customers could make the service hard for banks to ignore, despite UPI’s dominance.

Even if Apple Pay remains a niche service, the economics could still make India meaningful for Apple. The transaction fee the iPhone maker would charge would give it another way to monetize its growing base of iPhone users in the country, the people said.

At launch, eligible Axis Bank customers can add their credit cards to Apple’s Wallet app and use Apple Pay for online purchases as well as contactless payments at supported terminals, the people said.

An Apple Pay transaction could work at a terminal operated by an independent payments provider that has enabled the service but fail at another terminal whose acquiring bank has not, one of the people said. That could make acceptance uneven during the initial rollout, even for customers with supported cards.

The launch adds another piece to Apple’s growing business in India, where it has been expanding iPhone sales, local manufacturing, and its retail footprint. Apple accounted for 28% of India’s smartphone market by value in 2025, up from 23% a year earlier, per an earlier report by Counterpoint Research.

India already accounts for about a quarter of global iPhone production, and that share could rise to 30% to 35% over the next five years, Indian English daily Business Standard reported last month, citing an Indian government official.

Update: This story, originally published Tuesday morning, has been updated to reflect that the launch is now underway.

topStories.fullTranslation:
正如 TechCrunch 率先报道的那样，苹果于周二开始在印度推出 Apple Pay。其首家银行合作伙伴是该国第三大私营银行 Axis Bank。在经历了多年的推迟之后，此举将苹果的支付服务带入了这个全球人口最多的国家。在这个市场中，国家支持的统一支付接口（UPI）占据着主导地位。

初期的推广范围有限。Apple Pay 支持 Axis Bank 旗下的 Visa 和万事达（Mastercard）合规卡片，但不支持印度本土的 RuPay 网络。该服务的受理范围也将仅限于已启用该服务的商家和支付终端。

苹果表示，该服务将被全印度“数百万商家”受理，包括 Blinkit、Croma、Ixigo、信实（Reliance）旗下品牌、Tata 1mg 以及 Zomato。该公司已与包括 Cashfree、JusPay、Mswipe、Paytm、PayU、Pine Labs、Razorpay 和 Worldline 在内的支付服务商合作，以支持 Apple Pay 的受理。

与印度无处不在的统一支付接口（UPI）系统（该系统允许消费者在不依赖银行卡的情况下直接进行银行间即时转账）不同，Apple Pay 基于银行卡运作，需要各个发卡行和支付基础设施提供商与该服务进行系统整合。这使得大规模推广更加复杂。知情人士称，苹果的商业条款也成为与印度部分大型银行谈判的症结所在。

据知情人士透露，苹果要求对交易收取约 20 个基点（0.2%）的手续费，这在支付层约 40 到 50 个基点（0.4% 至 0.5%）的微薄利润中切走了一大块。知情人士表示，这一收费结构与 Apple Pay 在其他市场的商业模式大致相符。一位知情人士告诉 TechCrunch，由于有关商业条款的谈判仍在进行，HDFC Bank、ICICI Bank 和 SBI Card 在上线初期并未支持 Apple Pay。

苹果、Axis Bank、HDFC Bank、ICICI Bank 和 SBI Card 均未回应就此次上线置评的请求。本月早些时候，路透社报道称，苹果正准备于 10 月在印度推出 Apple Pay，首先支持 Axis Bank 信用卡。

Apple Pay 进军的支付市场与美国及其他重度依赖银行卡的经济体截然不同。印度的数字支付繁荣主要是由 UPI 推动的，这个国家支持的系统允许消费者直接在银行账户之间转移资金。

UPI 处理了印度绝大多数的数字支付，在印度，扫描二维码直接从银行账户付款已成常态。相比之下，Apple Pay 初期面向的是一个规模小得多的银行卡支付市场。

尽管如此，Apple Pay 可能会吸引印度日益增长的 iPhone 用户群，这些用户往往更为富裕，且更有可能使用高端信用卡。尽管 UPI 占据主导地位，但这些客户群体可能会让银行难以忽视这项服务。

即使 Apple Pay 仍然是一项小众服务，其商业效益仍可能使印度市场对苹果具有重大意义。知情人士表示，这家 iPhone 制造商收取的交易手续费将为其在该国不断扩大的 iPhone 用户群提供另一种变现途径。

知情人士称，上线后，合规的 Axis Bank 客户可以将其信用卡添加到苹果的钱包（Wallet）应用中，并使用 Apple Pay 进行在线购物，以及在受支持的终端上进行非接触式支付。

一位知情人士表示，在已启用该服务的独立支付服务商运营的终端上，Apple Pay 交易可以成功，但在收单银行尚未启用该服务的另一台终端上可能会失败。这可能会导致在初期推广阶段，即使持有受支持卡片的客户，其使用体验也可能不够均衡。

此次上线为苹果在印度不断增长的业务增添了新的拼图。苹果一直在印度扩大 iPhone 销售、本土制造以及零售业务布局。根据 Counterpoint Research 此前的一份报告，按销售额计算，苹果在 2025 年占印度智能手机市场的 28%，高于前一年的 23%。

印度英文日报《商业标准报》（Business Standard）上个月援引一名印度政府官员的话报道称，印度目前已占全球 iPhone 产量的约四分之一，未来五年内这一比例可能会上升至 30% 到 35%。

topStories.source: The Guardian Society (卫报社会与民生)

topStories.fullContent:
Councils collectively spent record 71.9% of core spending on adult and children’s care last year, analysis shows

Sixteen English councils spent more than 80% of their core funding on adult and children’s social care last year, highlighting the growing financial pressure on other local services.

Guardian analysis of government figures found that councils responsible for social care spent a net £42.8bn on adult and children’s services in 2025-26, equivalent to a record 71.9% of their combined core spending. Adult social care took 44.5% and children’s services accounted for 27.4%. In 2017-18, care costs made up 62.4% of councils’ core spending.
topStories.fullTranslation:
分析显示，地方议会去年在成年人和儿童照护上的支出创纪录地占到了核心支出的71.9%
英格兰有16个地方议会去年将其核心资金的80%以上用于成年人和儿童社会照护，突显出其他地方公共服务正面临日益严峻的财政压力。
《卫报》对政府数据的分析发现，负责社会照护的地方议会在2025-26年度用于成年人和儿童服务的净支出达428亿英镑，相当于其核心支出总额的71.9%，创历史新高。其中，成年人社会照护占44.5%，儿童服务占27.4%。而在2017-18年度，照护成本占地方议会核心支出的比例为62.4%。

So you we're looking for the RSS Feed of Last.fm, and then discovered they were gone!

Well, the solution is right here, all you have to do is tell me your username and i'll give you four URLs, one for you recent tracks, one for your loved ones, one for your top tracks and one for your top artists (the last two with an optional period, defaults to 1 month).

also new: images! if last.fm adds something other than a default image, it's large version is added as an enclosure

2025: Added support for recommended tracks. This comes bot in RSS as Soundixx-compatible JSON format.

period can be: 7day, 1month, 3month, 6month, 12month or overall

topStories.title: 新加坡淡马锡将扩大在中东业务版图，设立阿布扎比与利雅得办事处
topStories.originalTitle: Singapore's Temasek to expand Middle East presence, open Abu Dhabi, Riyadh offices
topStories.stance: 国际资本与华尔街视角
topStories.source: CNBC Markets (CNBC 市场官方英文)
topStories.snippet: Singapore state investor Temasek plans to open offices in Riyadh and Abu Dhabi by the first half of 2027, its most significant Mideast expansion to date.
topStories.fullContent:
Singaporean state-owned investor Temasek plans to open offices in Abu Dhabi and Riyadh, expanding its Middle East footprint as the region attracts capital despite the strain of the Iran war.

The $400 billion investor is betting on long-term opportunities created by the Gulf's economic transformation. But some flagship projects, particularly under Saudi Arabia's Vision 2030 program, have faced delays or revisions due to tighter finances, weaker foreign investment flows and economic fallout from the Iran war.

"The pace and ambition of economic transformation across the region are remarkable, and its long-term fundamentals remain highly attractive. We see strong alignment between the region's priorities and Temasek's own areas of focus," Dilhan Pillay Sandrasegara, Temasek's CEO, said in a press release shared with CNBC.

Temasek's Riyadh and Abu Dhabi offices, which are expected to open in the first half of 2027, will serve as hubs for the state investor and its network. Several of Temasek's partners in the region plan to co-locate in these hubs, according to the release.

Temasek is not new to the region. In 2025, the firm's $54 billion asset management arm Seviora opened an office in Abu Dhabi and signed a partnership with Mubadala Capital to pursue co-investment opportunities

In May of this year, Temasek teamed up with BlackRock's Global Infrastructure Partners, Abu Dhabi's L'IMAD and state owned-oil company ADNOC to target $30 billion in infrastructure deals across the Persian Gulf and Central Asia. The war in Iran has challenged Gulf energy infrastructure, straining exports from key producers and pushing Saudi Arabia, the UAE and Qatar to try and find alternate ways to export their crude and LNG.

Temasek will also "actively engage with institutions" in Qatar, according to a press release. The addition of offices in Riyadh and Abu Dhabi join the investor's 13 other locations around the globe spanning nine countries. The Middle East expansion brings that number to 11, along with hubs in China, India, Belgium, the U.S., Mexico and the U.K.

Chia Song Hwee, Temasek's Global Investments CEO and Middle East & Africa Chairman, will oversee Temasek's regional push, alongside Ankit Khemka who is managing director for the region, according to the release.

新加坡国有投资机构淡马锡（Temasek）计划在阿布扎比和利雅得设立办事处，尽管面临伊朗战争带来的压力，该地区仍在持续吸引资本，淡马锡正借此扩大其在中东的业务版图。

这家规模达4000亿美元的投资机构正押注海湾地区经济转型所带来的长期机遇。然而，受资金收紧、外国投资流入疲软以及伊朗战争引发的经济冲击影响，一些旗舰项目——尤其是沙特阿拉伯“2030愿景”计划下的项目——已面临延期或调整。

淡马锡首席执行官狄澜（Dilhan Pillay Sandrasegara）在与CNBC分享的新闻稿中表示：“整个地区经济转型的步伐和雄心令人瞩目，其长期基本面依然极具吸引力。我们看到该地区的发展优先事项与淡马锡自身的重点关注领域之间存在高度契合。”

根据新闻稿，淡马锡预计将于2027年上半年启用的利雅得与阿布扎比办事处，将作为该国有投资机构及其业务网络的区域枢纽。淡马锡在该地区的数家合作伙伴亦计划入驻这些枢纽协同办公。

淡马锡对该地区并不陌生。2025年，该公司旗下资产规模达540亿美元的资产管理子公司Seviora在阿布扎比设立了办事处，并与穆巴达拉资本（Mubadala Capital）签署了合作协议以寻求共同投资机会。

今年5月，淡马锡与贝莱德（BlackRock）旗下的全球基础设施合伙公司（Global Infrastructure Partners）、阿布扎比的L'IMAD以及阿联酋国有石油公司阿布扎比国家石油公司（ADNOC）携手，计划在波斯湾和中亚地区达成规模达300亿美元的基础设施交易。伊朗境内的战事对海湾地区的能源基础设施构成了严峻挑战，使主要产油国的出口承压，并促使沙特阿拉伯、阿联酋和卡塔尔寻求替代路径来出口其原油和液化天然气（LNG）。

新闻稿还称，淡马锡还将“积极与卡塔尔的机构开展接触”。利雅得与阿布扎比办事处的加入，使该投资机构在全球9个国家设立的13处分支网络进一步扩充。此次中东扩张使覆盖的国家总数达到11个，此外还包括中国、印度、比利时、美国、墨西哥和英国的业务枢纽。

根据新闻稿，淡马锡全球投资首席执行官兼中东及非洲区主席谢松辉（Chia Song Hwee）将与该地区董事总经理安基特·凯姆卡（Ankit Khemka）共同统筹淡马锡在当地的扩张布局。

topStories.title: 完美“爪”选：澳大利亚找到新一代考拉救援犬
topStories.originalTitle: Paw-fect candidate: Australia finds new koala rescue dog
topStories.snippet: The hunt is over: After trawling through dozens of applications, an Australian animal welfare group has found a successor to a hero hound credited with saving more than 100 koalas from fires.
topStories.fullContent:
edited by Alexander Pol

This article has been reviewed according to Science X's editorial process and policies. Editors have highlighted the following attributes while ensuring the content's credibility:

reputable news agency

The hunt is over: After trawling through dozens of applications, an Australian animal welfare group has found a successor to a hero hound credited with saving more than 100 koalas from fires.

Bear surrendered his collar in March after a decade of being a very good boy as one of the first dogs in the country to be trained to detect the scent of koala fur.

Those skills were critical in helping rescuers find marsupial survivors of wildfires.

With Bear's retirement, the International Fund for Animal Welfare launched a search for his successor, admitting: "He's leaving very big boots to fill."

Among dozens of applications from across the country—and as far afield as the United States—an Australian koolie called Oaka stood out.

"We didn't know it would be possible to find a new Bear. He was truly one of a kind ... but then along came Oaka," said Josey Sharrad, the welfare fund's Oceania head of programs.

"Bear showed the world what's possible when a rescue dog is given a second chance and finds its true purpose. I see that same spark in Oaka."

Oaka, like Bear, was considered "too much to handle" by her family, the group said.

But her potential was spotted by a local rescue group, which submitted an application. She then passed the initial test "with flying colors."

The animal welfare group's director of canine units, Frederic Chappee, said Oaka was "almost too good to be true."

"For many people around the world, Bear became an icon. But what makes Bear truly unique is not only what he achieved, but the void he left behind. It's a void that I am hopeful Oaka can fill," he said.

Bear's skills saved over 100 koalas as the Black Summer wildfires raged across Australia's eastern seaboard from late 2019 to early 2020, razing millions of hectares, destroying thousands of homes and blanketing cities in noxious smoke.

With Australia's fire services warning that the start of the Southern Hemisphere summer later this year could see more intense blazes, Oaka's training will be fast-tracked.

"We know how critical it is to have a highly skilled koala detection dog back in the field, helping protect one of Australia's most iconic species," Sharrad said.

"With El Niño already here and a tough summer on the horizon, our koalas will need all the help they can get, whether it comes on two legs or four."

寻觅之旅画上句号：在仔细筛选了数十份申请之后，一家澳大利亚动物福利机构为一只曾从野火中拯救了100多只考拉的功勋犬找到了继任者。

作为全澳首批接受考拉毛皮气味搜寻训练的搜救犬之一，名为“熊”（Bear）的搜救犬在恪尽职守长达十年后，于今年3月光荣退役并卸下项圈。

这些专业技能对于协助救援人员在山火后搜寻幸存的有袋类动物至关重要。

随着 Bear 的退役，国际爱护动物基金会（IFAW）启动了寻找继任者的行动，并坦言：“要填补他留下的空缺极其不易。”

在来自全澳各地乃至远至美国的数十份申请中，一只名为 Oaka 的澳大利亚库利犬（Australian koolie）脱颖而出。

“我们曾不知道是否还能找到另一只像 Bear 一样的搜救犬。他确实是独一无二的……但随后 Oaka 出现了，”该动物福利基金会大洋洲项目负责人乔西·沙拉德（Josey Sharrad）表示。

“Bear 向世界展示了，当一只曾被救助的流浪犬获得重获新生的机会并找到真正的使命时，会创造出怎样的可能。我在 Oaka 身上看到了同样的闪光点。”

该机构表示，Oaka 和 Bear 一样，曾经也因过于活泼好动而被原收养家庭认为“难以管教”。

不过，当地一家动物救助组织发现了她的潜能并提交了申请。随后，她以优异成绩顺利通过了初步考核。

该动物福利机构犬类部门负责人弗雷德里克·夏佩（Frederic Chappee）表示，Oaka 的表现“完美得令人难以置信”。

“对全世界许多人来说，Bear 已经成为一个标志性象征。但让 Bear 真正与众不同的不仅是他的成就，还有他退役后留下的空白。我非常希望 Oaka 能够填补这一空白，”他说。

2019年末至2020年初，澳大利亚东海岸爆发了灾难性的“黑色夏季”（Black Summer）山火，大火吞噬了数百万公顷土地，摧毁了数千所房屋，有毒浓烟笼罩多座城市。在那场危机中，Bear 凭借出色本领挽救了100多只考拉的生命。

鉴于澳大利亚消防部门警告称，今年晚些指南半球夏季开始时可能会面临更猛烈的火势，Oaka 的实战训练进程将大幅提速。

“我们深知，让一只技能精湛的考拉搜寻犬重返野外一线、协助保护这一澳大利亚最具代表性的物种具有何等关键的意义，”沙拉德说。

“随着厄尔尼诺现象已经到来，严峻的夏季即将来临，我们的考拉将需要所有能获得的一切帮助，无论这份援助是来自两条腿的人类还是四条腿的动物伙伴。”

topStories.originalTitle: 东航回应“合肥至大连航班空中服务事件”：第一时间对当事乘务员开展心理疏导
topStories.snippet: 中新网9月30日电 中国东方航空在其官方微博发文称，公司关注到网传9月28日合肥至大连航班空中服务事件相关视频。经核实，航班乘务员在推餐车提供饮料服务过程中，全程提示旅客注意，因一名旅客处于睡眠状态，不慎造成餐车与其手肘发生触碰。乘务员当即反复致歉，查看旅客状况。该旅客情绪激动，连续使用粗俗过激言语，并出现威胁脚踢乘务员、要求当事乘务员落地后陪同就医等言行，该乘务员受到惊吓。为维护飞行安全和客舱秩序，乘务长、安全员迅速介入协同处置。航班落地后，医护人员上机检查旅客未有明显外伤或肿胀、无须进一步处理，旅客拒绝地面人员陪同送医，自行离开。

中新网9月30日电 中国东方航空在其官方微博发文称，公司关注到网传9月28日合肥至大连航班空中服务事件相关视频。经核实，航班乘务员在推餐车提供饮料服务过程中，全程提示旅客注意，因一名旅客处于睡眠状态，不慎造成餐车与其手肘发生触碰。乘务员当即反复致歉，查看旅客状况。该旅客情绪激动，连续使用粗俗过激言语，并出现威胁脚踢乘务员、要求当事乘务员落地后陪同就医等言行，该乘务员受到惊吓。为维护飞行安全和客舱秩序，乘务长、安全员迅速介入协同处置。航班落地后，医护人员上机检查旅客未有明显外伤或肿胀、无须进一步处理，旅客拒绝地面人员陪同送医，自行离开。

事件发生后，该公司第一时间对当事乘务员开展心理疏导与关怀支持，该员工已恢复正常工作。在此，对关心支持民航一线员工的旅客、公众表示感谢，公司正协同相关方对事件过程进行全面复盘取证。

topStories.fullContent: (ANSA) - ROME, 30 SET - Two of Eni's main rivals on the Italian utility market have said their prices are already lower after the State-controlled energy giant announced Tuesday that it will offer a 30% discount on electricity and gas bills starting in October for customers who sign up by the 24th of the month via its Plenitude subsidiary. It said the offer would save households struggling with soaring energy costs after prices spiked following the Iran war around 200 euros a year - 100 euros for gas and another 100 for electricity. Enel said its 'Digital Luce' offer for electricity featuring a 50% discount on the energy component of bills with respect to the wholesale price remained the lowest among the mayor players on the Italian market. A2A said it has been offering customers the chance to set the prices they pay fixed for 10 years at rates that are 50% below the current wholesale price since 2023. On Monday Eni also introduced a cap for its gas stations, limiting prices at €2.19 per litre for diesel and €1.99 for unleaded petrol for a month. Kuwait's Q8 and Azerbaijan's SOCAR with its IP chain have said they will cap prices at their gas stations too. Premier Giorgia Meloni has thanked the companies for introducing these limits. (ANSA).
topStories.fullTranslation: （安莎社）- 罗马，9月30日 - 在意大利国家控股的能源巨头埃尼集团（Eni）于周二宣布将从10月起为在当月24日前通过其子公司Plenitude签约的用户提供30%的电费和燃气费折扣后，该国公用事业市场上的两家埃尼主要竞争对手表示，它们的价格早已更低。埃尼表示，这项优惠每年将为因伊朗战争后价格飙升而饱受高昂能源成本困扰的家庭节省约200欧元——燃气费和电费各节省100欧元。意大利国家电力公司（Enel）表示，其名为“Digital Luce”的供电方案对账单中的能源组成部分提供相对于批发价50%的折扣，仍是意大利市场上主要企业中价格最低的。A2A公司则表示，自2023年以来，该公司便一直向客户提供将其支付价格锁定10年的选择，锁定费率比当前批发价低50%。周一，埃尼还在其加油站推行了限价措施，在一个月内将柴油价格限制在每升2.19欧元，无铅汽油价格限制在每升1.99欧元。科威特Q8石油公司以及阿塞拜疆国家石油公司（SOCAR）及其IP连锁加油站也表示，它们也将对旗下加油站实行限价。意大利总理焦尔吉娅·梅洛尼对各企业推行这些限制举措表示了感谢。（安莎社）

topStories.fullContent: Crude oil prices ticked higher today, after dipping on Tuesday, following reports that President Trump has no intention of easing sanction pressure on Iran, which has decimated exports from one of OPEC’s biggest producers. At the time of writing, Brent crude was trading at $103.13 per barrel, and West Texas Intermediate was trading at $89.53, both set to end the month with a gain. For Brent, the gain is more pronounced, at around $10 per barrel, while for WTI, the gain would be about $3 per barrel. Earlier in the week, prices dipped slightly on the news that oil flows from the Persian Gulf have recovered to a level close to pre-war daily averages but there appear to be doubts about whether the recovery is sustainable. “Continued uncertainty over sanctions relief and negotiations is keeping a geopolitical risk premium embedded in prices,” analyst Sugandha Sachdeva, founder of India-based SS WealthStreet said, as quoted by Reuters. “Improving supplies could cap further gains, but renewed disruption or an escalation in tensions could ‌trigger another rally,” Sachdeva added. Data from Kpler has suggested oil exports from the Persian Gulf have rebounded strongly this month, with Hormuz flows alone at 13.2 million barrels daily, or 77% of pre-war levels, CNBC reported this week. An earlier report by Reuters citing Kpler data as well, pegged Hormuz flows specifically at 7.4 million barrels daily, with total Middle East oil export rates at 12.8 million barrels daily. “Despite more vessel traffic through the Strait of ‌Hormuz, flows remain below pre-conflict levels, keeping the market undersupplied,” UBS’ commodity analyst Giovanni Staunovo said, as quoted by the publication. It could be this shortfall that is keeping oil prices elevated, in addition to the still present risk for tankers in the Strait of Hormuz, in spite of the export recovery.  By Irina Slav for Oilprice.com
topStories.fullTranslation:
在周二出现回落后，原油价格今日小幅走高。此前有报道称，特朗普总统无意减轻对伊朗的制裁压力，而该制裁已经重创了这个欧佩克（OPEC）主要产油国之一的出口。截至发稿时，布伦特原油交易价格为每桶103.13美元，西得克萨斯中质原油（WTI）交易价格为每桶89.53美元，两者本月均势将收涨。对于布伦特原油而言，其涨势更为明显，约为每桶10美元；而WTI原油的涨幅约为每桶3美元。

本周早些时候，有消息称来自波斯湾的原油运输量已恢复至接近战前日均水平，油价随之轻微走低，但市场对这种恢复是否具有可持续性显然存有疑虑。路透社援引印度SS WealthStreet创始人、分析师苏甘达·萨赫德瓦（Sugandha Sachdeva）的观点指出：“围绕制裁减免和谈判的持续不确定性，使得地缘政治风险溢价始终体现在价格之中。”萨赫德瓦补充称：“供应改善可能会限制油价进一步上涨，但若是出现新的供应中断或紧张局势加剧，可能会引发新一轮上涨行情。”

据CNBC本周报道，Kpler的数据显示，波斯湾本月的石油出口强劲反弹，仅霍尔木兹海峡的日均通航流量就达1320万桶，即战前水平的77%。路透社此前同样援引Kpler数据的一篇报道则将霍尔木兹海峡的具体流量标定在每日740万桶，中东石油总出口率则为每日1280万桶。瑞银集团（UBS）大宗商品分析师乔瓦尼·斯陶诺沃（Giovanni Staunovo）在该报道中表示：“尽管通过霍尔木兹海峡的船舶流量有所增加，但流量仍低于冲突前水平，从而使市场维持供不应求的状态。”除了霍尔木兹海峡油轮即便在出口恢复的情况下依然面临潜在风险之外，可能正是这一供应缺口支撑了油价的高企。

文/伊琳娜·斯拉夫（Irina Slav），Oilprice.com

topStories.title: 北京警告：若欧洲对中国企业施加限制将予以反击
topStories.originalTitle: Beijing warns of retaliation if Europe imposes curbs on Chinese businesses
topStories.stance: 国际资本与华尔街视角
topStories.source: CNBC Markets (CNBC 市场官方英文)
topStories.snippet: China must "respond firmly" if the EU introduces restrictions on Chinese businesses or products, the Commerce Ministry said, according to a CNBC translation.
topStories.fullContent:
BEIJING — China's commerce ministry has sent a strong warning to the European Union ahead of expected high-level talks in Beijing next week.

China will "respond firmly" if the EU introduces restrictions on Chinese businesses or products, the Chinese commerce ministry said in a statement late Tuesday, according to a CNBC translation of Mandarin.

The ministry said such actions, while China and the EU are engaged in trade talks, would "seriously undermine mutual trust" and "disrupt" the negotiations.

China and the EU have been engaged in trade talks this summer as Europe wants to reduce its record trade deficit with China by October. EU Trade Commissioner Maroš Šefčovič had warned in an interview with Euronews this week that Beijing must deliver "concrete results" by October or face "harsher measures." He is expected to visit Beijing next week.

Earlier this week, Rhodium Group's Noah Barkin said Europe was considering measures to shut China out of the bloc.

Citing European officials, he said Germany and France are finalizing a joint paper that calls on the European Commission to speed up development of a tool that one official described as allowing Brussels "to cut China off from the European market within 24 hours."

Barkin said the measures could mirror the U.S. Section 301 tariff approach. China's commerce ministry statement said it was responding to Europe's consideration of "301"-style tools.

While the Association of Southeast Asian Nations surpassed the EU in 2020 to become China's biggest goods trading partner, the EU's trade deficit with China is the largest in the world, recently surpassing the U.S. That's according to China Customs data accessed through Wind Information.

When including services, the EU said it was China's top trading partner, with combined trade of 880 billion euros, or nearly $1 trillion, last year.

北京——在中国商务部预计于下周在北京举行高级别会谈前夕，该部向欧盟发出了严厉警告。

根据CNBC对中文声明的翻译，中国商务部周二晚间在一份声明中表示，如果欧盟对中国企业或产品出台限制措施，中国将“坚决回应”。

该部表示，在中欧双方正进行贸易谈判之际采取此类行动，将“严重破坏互信”并“扰乱”谈判进程。

今年夏天，中欧一直在进行贸易谈判，因为欧洲希望在10月前削减其对华创纪录的贸易逆差。欧盟贸易专员马罗什·谢夫乔维奇（Maroš Šefčovič）本周在接受欧洲新闻台（Euronews）采访时警告称，北京必须在10月前拿出“实质性成果”，否则将面临“更严厉的措施”。他预计将于下周访问北京。

本周早些时候，荣鼎咨询（Rhodium Group）的诺亚·巴尔金（Noah Barkin）表示，欧洲正考虑采取措施将中国排除在欧盟市场之外。

他援引欧洲官员的话称，德国和法国正在敲定一份联合文件，呼吁欧盟委员会加快研发一种工具，一名官员将其描述为可允许布鲁塞尔“在24小时内切断中国与欧洲市场的联系”。

巴尔金表示，这些措施可能会仿效美国的“301条款”关税手段。中国商务部声明表示，此番表态正是针对欧洲考虑出台“301”式工具的回应。

尽管东南亚国家联盟（东盟）在2020年超过欧盟成为中国最大的货物贸易伙伴，但欧盟对华贸易逆差位居全球首位，最近更超过了美国。这一数据来自通过万得资讯（Wind）获取的中国海关数据。

如果计入服务贸易，欧盟方面表示其去年是中国最大的贸易伙伴，双边综合贸易额达到8800亿欧元（近1万亿美元）。

topStories.title: 弗兰克·埃尔德森：监管风险偏好、效率与有效性
topStories.originalTitle: Frank Elderson: Supervisory risk appetite, efficiency and effectiveness
topStories.source: European Central Bank (欧洲央行官方英文)
topStories.fullContent:
Bali, 30 September 2026

Banks are operating in an increasingly complex environment shaped by geopolitical fragmentation, rapid technological change, volatile energy and commodity prices, rising inflation, demographic changes, growing interconnectedness with non-bank financial institutions, and persistent climate and nature-related risks. What does it take for supervisors to remain effective and impactful in this new reality?

The challenge facing supervisors today is not simply that there are more risks. Rather, the risk landscape is increasingly uncertain, interconnected and volatile. But this does not mean that supervisors should try to monitor everything, everywhere, all at once. Quite the opposite. In a more complex world, effective supervision requires clearer, forward-looking prioritisation. In European banking supervision, we have therefore been adapting how we supervise. Our approach rests on three mutually reinforcing pillars: sharper risk prioritisation, simpler and more efficient supervision and timely remediation.

We have learned – often the hard way when crises hit – that simply complying with minimum capital requirements is not enough to ensure banks remain safe and sound. The 2023 banking turmoil reminded us that banks can meet all of the formal capital and liquidity requirements, while underlying weaknesses in governance, risk culture or business models nonetheless continue to accumulate beneath the surface, until it’s too late[1]. In our supervision we therefore focus on material risks wherever they arise – be they risks to capital or liquidity, governance, operational resilience or structural risk drivers like climate and nature related or geopolitical risks.[2]

However, we must challenge the assumption that effective supervision means looking at every single risk, in every bank, in every detail and do this every year. Supervisors simply cannot operate with a zero-risk-tolerance mindset.

Through our dedicated risk tolerance framework (RTF), we have consciously increased our supervisory risk tolerance. Risk-based supervision helps determine where supervisory attention should be focused. The RTF goes one step further: it clarifies how much residual supervisory risk can be accepted when certain areas are reviewed less intensively or deferred. This is an important point because de-prioritisation is not a passive outcome or a resource-driven omission. It is an active and conscious supervisory judgment, made within an institutional framework and supported by a culture that empowers supervisors to focus on what matters most. In practice, this means that lower-priority risk areas at individual banks are not subject to the same intensive supervisory scrutiny every year.

Put simply: in a more complex risk environment, supervisors must become more focused if they want to remain effective. The impact of this approach is already emerging, albeit that, naturally, it will take some time before the full effects are felt.

But a culture shift towards greater risk appetite – one that prioritises substance over form – is not something supervisors can deliver in isolation. As the European Commission rightly highlighted in its recent report on banking competitiveness,[3] creating a less risk averse and more agile environment is a shared responsibility. All stakeholders, including banks, must be willing to be part of this cultural shift and take more responsibility for applying the law based on materiality. This means that also banks need to play their part by refraining from continuous demands for guidance in search of an ever-higher degree of legal certainty.

A simpler and less prescriptive framework places even greater weight on supervisory judgement, not less. Regulation alone cannot fully capture in every precision every emerging risk or idiosyncratic business model. Any attempt to do so would result in an increasingly complex rulebook and could create new opportunities for regulatory arbitrage. Strong supervisory judgement, and the willingness to act when risks are not adequately managed, are therefore more important than ever.

The second pillar of effective supervision is greater efficiency.

For example as part of our Next Level Supervision initiative, we have reviewed supervisory processes from end to end to identify where we can move faster, reduce duplication and ask only for information that is strictly necessary.[4]

Let me be clear: this is not only about trimming down procedures. It is a way to cut down on undue complexity and free up supervisory capacity for a more focused assessment of material risks, without lowering guardrails or weakening resilience.

It is about delivering the same level of safety and soundness with a framework that is easier to navigate for both banks and supervisors.

And we are already seeing tangible results.

For example, we have reviewed more than 100 supervisory guidance publications to make them more concise and user-friendly.[5] Around 40 have been discontinued, while others have been revised in a targeted manner and several are undergoing a more in-depth review.

Or take the approval of simple securitisation transactions. As part of our simplification work we have reduced processing days for standardised and less risky securitisations from three months to an average of around seven days.

We have also reduced stress testing data points by around 55%, shortened turnaround times in fit-and-proper assessments through digitalisation and AI-enabled tools, and reduced approval timelines for capital related decision from several months to less than six days.

In sum, our simplification activities have already started to yield tangible benefits, and we will continue rolling out these initiatives throughout the year. The aim is simple: more focus on material risks, while preserving only the necessary procedural safeguards

But increasing risk appetite and efficiency are only part of the story.

Ultimately, effective supervision is not only about the material risks it identifies, but about whether banks address those risks in a timely manner and lasting effect.

Supervision must lead to change where change is needed. Supervisors need to have the powers, ability and willingness to act to make sure that findings are addressed in good time. And when they have the powers, ability and willingness to act, when the circumstances require so supervisors should indeed do just that: act. And not just act: act in time and with the appropriate degree of forcefulness and tenacity. The March 2023 banking turmoil underscored how costly delays can be when known weaknesses remain unresolved. This is also a point on which the various IMF and BCBS post-mortem reports are all in agreement.[6]

A structured escalation framework is essential to driving concrete change at banks. Supervisors must set out remediation paths that are proportionate, time-bound and root-cause-oriented – and they must be prepared to timely escalate to enforcement measures when necessary. Timely remediation is not enough if it remains superficial. Findings need to be addressed durably, at the level of the underlying weaknesses that gave rise to them, whether these relate to banks’ governance, risk management, internal controls or business model. By remedying root causes, not only current, but also possible future manifestations of such root causes are addressed, thus killing many birds with one stone.

And to do that, supervisors need a comprehensive toolkit, including capital requirements but also qualitative measures That, when appropriate, can require banks to change governance, controls, processes, risk management or business-model practices. For example, European banking supervision uses qualitative requirements widely and the requirements span from requiring banks to reinforce risk management to imposing business restrictions or periodic penalty payments as an enforcement tool. Each of these instruments has an important place in the supervisory toolkit, and supervisors must be prepared to use the right tools at the right time,[7] considering the materiality of the weakness, the persistence of the issue as well as the bank’s responsiveness.

Policymakers are increasingly focusing on growth and competitiveness. How can international standards and supervisory cooperation help ensure that these objectives are pursued in a way that supports financial stability, rather than undermining it?

The starting point is to recognise that growth, banking sector competitiveness and financial stability are not competing objectives. In fact, they reinforce one another.

A resilient banking system is a precondition for sustainable economic growth. The global financial crisis showed very clearly that when financial stability is undermined, the costs to the real economy can be substantial and long-lasting.[8] And, more recently, the pandemic, the energy shock following Russia’s invasion of Ukraine and the conflict in the Middle East have all shown that a resilient banking sector can support the economy in challenging times.

Ultimately, banking sector competitiveness cannot be captured by a single metric, such as profitability.[9] Competitiveness depends on whether banks are resilient, efficient and innovative, and whether they can deploy new technologies quickly and effectively. Simply reducing prudential standards and capital requirements is no guarantee of greater competitiveness or lending. It would reduce resilience and could just as easily result in more share buybacks and higher distribution to shareholders. In other words, strong prudential standards are not an obstacle to competitiveness. They are one of its foundations.

The real question is therefore not whether we need strong standards, but how we can make them as

effective, proportionate and coherent as possible. This is where international standards play an important role in safeguarding resilience and maintaining a level playing field across jurisdictions.

If we did not already have a Basel Committee on Banking Supervision and a Financial Stability Board, the current geopolitical fragmentation would be a compelling reason to create them. International standards act as a common foundation. They establish minimum expectations while preserving flexibility for local implementation. But there is a strong case for avoiding unnecessary divergence, particularly where banks operate across multiple markets. A fragmented regulatory landscape may create a race to the bottom while adding complexity and costs. The timely and full implementation of Basel III therefore remains critical.

At the same time, as we simplify the prudential framework and improve coordination between authorities, we must preserve one of the defining strengths of effective supervision: the ability to identify and address risks at individual banks. Common rules provide an essential and risk-based foundation, while banks can differ materially in their business models, governance, controls and exposure to emerging risks. Supervisors therefore need sufficient scope to use bank-specific qualitative and quantitative measures where warranted.

The same applies to supervisory cooperation. The risks we face are global – they don’t stop at borders. Tackling them effectively requires coordination and cooperation among authorities.

The rapid growth of the non-bank financial sector provides an illustration. The sector has doubled in size since 2008 and now accounts for over half of financial sector assets in the euro area. Yet parts of the sector remain comparatively opaque. Data gaps and limited transparency can make it difficult to fully assess how risks may spread between banks and non-banks during periods of stress. That’s why we are calling for greater transparency and better reporting for actors on private markets. We need international policy responses to ensure that pockets of vulnerability are adequately addressed.[10]

But, increasingly, risks also demand cooperation beyond prudential authorities.

Take cyber resilience. The emergence of increasingly sophisticated AI-enabled cyberattacks is a gamechanger in the threat landscape. The speed, scale and accessibility of advanced cyber capabilities are increasing rapidly. This is why European banking supervision is working closely on strengthening banks’ operational resilience to cyber risks, not only with the banks themselves, but also with cybersecurity authorities.

And the challenge to banks’ operational resilience does not stop with AI. Quantum computing is already appearing on the horizon and could become widely available by 2030. Quantum risk to cryptography is already a risk as sensitive, encrypted information can be collected today and stored with the expectation that future technological advances may allow it to be decrypted in a “harvest now, decrypt later” fashion. To stay ahead of these developments, supervisors increasingly need to engage with experts far beyond the financial sector.

The same applies to the risks from the ongoing climate and nature crises. To better model the transmission channels of climate and nature-related risks to the economy and banks’ balance sheets, we are increasingly teaming up with the scientific community, including climate scientists and biodiversity experts.

The risk landscape is evolving rapidly. New technologies are emerging, existing risks are changing in nature, scale and speed, and financial systems are becoming increasingly interconnected. Cooperation is therefore not merely a perk – it is a necessity. International standards and supervisory cooperation are essential if we are to support growth and competitiveness while preserving the financial stability on which both ultimately depend.

For more details on supervisory risk appetite statements in different jurisdictions, see Balan, M. and Zamil, R. (2026), “Acting under uncertainty – the case for supervisory risk appetite frameworks”, FSI Insights on policy implementation, No 74, Bank for International Settlements, May.

For why a broader view on resilience, including governance and risk culture, operational resilience and structural risk drivers are not peripheral issues but are at the core of prudential supervision, see Elderson, F. (2025), “What good supervision looks like”, keynote speech at the 24th Annual International Conference on Policy Challenges for the Financial Sector, Washington DC, 12 June; and Elderson, F. (2025), “Resilience offers a competitive advantage, especially in uncertain times”, keynote speech at the Morgan Stanley European Financials Conference, London, 19 March.

European Commission (2026), Communication on the Competitiveness of the Banking Sector and the Single Market in Banking, July.

For an overview of the SSM’s simplification work, please see Donnery, S. and Amis, P. (2026), “Streamlining supervision, safeguarding resilience: tangible progress on our reform agenda”, The Supervision Blog, ECB, 6 July.

Elderson, F. (2026), “Simpler guidance, more effective supervision”, The Supervision Blog, ECB, 26 June.

For further information on supervisory effectiveness please read the following speeches in conjuncture: Elderson, F. (2023), “Powers, ability and willingness to act – the mainstay of effective banking supervision”, speech at the House of the Euro Brussels, 7 December. “What good supervision looks like”, keynote speech at the 24th Annual International Conference on Policy Challenges for the Financial Sector, Washington DC, 12 June

The great financial crisis remains the biggest growth-destroying event in modern economic history. In Europe, previous systemic financial crises had resulted in average output losses of 8.5% of GDP in EU countries. See Lo Duca, M. et al. (2017), “A new database for financial crises in European countries”, Occasional Paper Series, No 194, ECB, July; and Woods, S. (2024), “Competing for growth”, speech at the Annual City Banquet, Mansion House, 17 October.

According to supervisory data, euro area banks’ return on equity has recovered significantly and stabilised at over 10%, reaching some of the highest levels observed since the establishment of the Single Supervisory Mechanism (SSM). Investors are increasingly recognising this progress. The valuation gap with US banks has narrowed significantly, with the average price-to-book ratio of European banks now close to 1.5. This demonstrates an important point: resilience, competitiveness and profitability are not conflicting objectives for banks.

Financial Stability Board (2025), Global Monitoring Report on Nonbank Financial Intermediation, 16 December.

巴厘岛，2026年9月30日

银行业正处在一个日益复杂的环境中，这一环境受到地缘政治碎片化、快速技术变革、能源与大宗商品价格波动、通胀上升、人口结构变化、与非银金融机构关联度日益加深，以及持续存在的气候和自然相关风险的影响。在这一新现实下，监管机构如何才能保持有效性并发挥实质影响力？

如今监管机构面临的挑战，不仅在于风险数量的增加，更在于风险格局日益呈现出高度的不确定性、互联性和波动性。但这并不意味着监管机构应当试图在同一时间、对所有机构的方方面面进行全天候监控。恰恰相反，在更加复杂的世界中，有效的监管需要更加明确、具有前瞻性的优先级排序。因此，在欧洲银行监管框架下，我们一直在调整监管方式。我们的监管方法立足于三大相辅相成的支柱：更精准的风险优先级排序、更简便高效的监管流程，以及更及时的整改落实。

我们已经吸取了教训——往往是在危机爆发时付出了惨痛代价才认识到——仅仅遵守最低资本要求不足以确保银行的稳健与安全。2023年的银行业动荡提醒我们，银行即使满足了所有的形式资本与流动性要求，其在公司治理、风险文化或商业模式方面的潜在弱点仍可能在表象之下不断累积，直至为时过晚[1]。因此，在我们的日常监管中，无论重大风险出现在哪里，我们都会予以重点关注——不论是资本或流动性风险、治理风险、运营韧性风险，还是诸如气候与自然相关风险或地缘政治风险等结构性风险驱动因素[2]。

然而，我们必须破除这样一种假设，即认为有效监管就等于每年都要对每家银行的每一项风险、每一个细节都进行全面审查。监管机构绝不能以零风险容忍的心态来开展工作。

通过专门制定的风险容忍框架（RTF），我们有意识地提高了监管风险容忍度。基于风险的监管有助于确定监管注意力应当投向何处。而风险容忍框架更进一步：它明确了当对某些领域的审查力度降低或予以推迟时，监管层可以接受多大程度的残留监管风险。这是一个重要原则，因为降低优先级并不是一种被动的结果，也不是由于资源不足而造成的疏漏。它是在制度框架之内作出的一项主动而自觉的监管判断，并得到赋权监管人员专注于最重要事务的文化支撑。在实践中，这意味着个别银行较低优先级的风险领域，不再需要每年都接受同样高强度的监管审查。

简而言之：在更加复杂的风险环境中，监管机构如果希望保持有效性，就必须变得更加聚焦。这种方法的影响力已初步显现，尽管其全部效果的显现自然还需要一定时间。

但是，向更高风险偏好转变的文化转向——一种注重实质重于形式的转变——并不是监管机构单方面就能实现的。正如欧盟委员会在最近关于银行业竞争力的报告中所恰当强调的[3]，营造一个不那么厌恶风险、更加灵活敏捷的环境是一项共同的责任。包括银行在内的所有利益相关方，都必须乐于融入这一文化转变，并承担更多基于实质重要性适用法律法规的责任。这也意味着银行需要发挥自身作用，停止为了追求极致的法律确定性而不断索要指导意见的做法。

一个更简单、规范性较弱的框架，对监管判断力的要求更高，而非更低。仅凭规则本身不可能精准捕捉到每一种新兴风险或独特的商业模式。任何试图这样做的做法都会导致规章制度日益繁冗复杂，并可能为监管套利创造新的空间。因此，强有力的监管判断力以及在风险未得到充分管理时果断行动的意愿，比以往任何时候都更加关键。

有效监管的第二大支柱是更高的效率。

例如，作为“下一阶段监管”（Next Level Supervision）举措的一部分，我们对监管流程进行了端到端审查，以找出可以提速、减少重复并仅索取绝对必要信息的环节[4]。

我要明确指出：这不仅仅是简化程序。它是一种消除不必要的复杂性、释放监管能力以便更聚焦于重大风险评估的手段，同时绝不会降低防线或削弱韧性。

其核心在于，通过一个让银行和监管机构都更易遵循的框架，实现相同水准的安全与稳健。

我们已经看到了切实成效。

例如，我们审查了100多份监管指导文件，使其更加简练、更便于使用[5]。其中约40份已废止，另有一些文件进行了针对性修订，还有数份正在接受更深度的审查。

又如简单证券化交易的审批。作为我们简化流程工作的一部分，我们将标准化、较低风险的证券化审批时间从三个月缩短至平均约七天左右。

我们还将压力测试的数据点缩减了约55%，通过数字化和人工智能工具缩短了高管任职资格审查的周期，并将资本相关决策的审批时限从数月缩短至六天以内。

总之，我们的简化举措已经开始产生切实的效益，我们将在全年继续推进这些举措。目标很简单：更加聚焦重大风险，同时仅保留必要的程序保障。

但提高风险偏好和效率只是整个蓝图的一部分。

归根结底，有效监管不仅取决于其识别出的重大风险，还取决于银行能否以具有长效机制的方式及时化解这些风险。

监管必须在需要变革的地方推动变革。监管人员需要具备行动的权力、能力和意愿，以确保发现的问题得到及时处置。当他们拥有行动的权力、能力和意愿，且客观环境有所要求时，监管人员确实应当果断采取行动。不仅要行动，而且要及时行动，并展现出应有的力度与韧性。2023年3月的银行业动荡深刻印证了已知缺陷若迟迟得不到解决会带来多么高昂的代价。这也是国际货币基金组织（IMF）和巴塞尔银行监管委员会（BCBS）各项事后总结报告中达成完全共识的一点[6]。

结构化的升级应对框架对于推动银行发生切实转变至关重要。监管机构必须制定相称、有时限且以根因治理为导向的整改路径——并且必须做好在必要时及时升级采取执法措施的准备。如果整改停留在表面，即便及时也是不够的。审查发现的问题必须在产生这些问题的深层缺陷层面上得到持久解决，无论这些缺陷是涉及银行的治理结构、风险管理、内部控制还是商业模式。通过消除根本诱因，不仅能够解决当前的表现形式，还能防范该诱因在未来的潜在表现，从而达到一举多得的效果。

为此，监管机构需要一个全面的工具箱，不仅包括资本要求，还包括定性监管措施，这些措施在适当情况下可要求银行改变其治理、控制机制、业务流程、风险管理或商业模式实践。例如，欧洲银行监管广泛应用定性要求，其范围涵盖从要求银行加强风险管理，到采取业务限制或处以定期罚金作为执法手段。在监管工具箱中，每一项工具都占据重要位置；考虑到缺陷的严重性、问题的持续性以及银行的响应程度，监管机构必须随时准备在适当时机使用恰当的工具。[7]

决策者正日益关注增长与竞争力。国际标准与监管合作如何能够帮助确保在追求这些目标的同时维护金融稳定，而非削弱金融稳定？

切入点在于认识到：增长、银行业竞争力和金融稳定并不是相互冲突的目标。事实上，它们是相辅相成的。

具备韧性的银行体系是经济可持续增长的前提条件。全球金融危机极其清晰地表明，当金融稳定遭到破坏时，实体经济承受的代价可能十分巨大且深远持久。[8] 近期，疫情、俄罗斯入侵乌克兰引发的能源冲击以及中东地区的冲突也都表明，具有韧性的银行业能够在充满挑战的时期为经济提供支撑。

归根结底，银行业的竞争力无法用单一指标（例如盈利能力）来衡量。[9] 竞争力取决于银行是否具备韧性、效率和创新能力，以及能否快速有效地部署新技术。单纯降低审慎标准和资本要求并不能保证提高竞争力或扩大放贷。这不仅会降低银行体系的韧性，还极易直接导致更多的股票回购和向股东分配更多利润。换句话说，严格的审慎标准不是竞争力的障碍，而是其基石之一。

因此，真正的问题不在于我们是否需要严格的标准，而在于我们如何使这些标准尽可能有效、相称且连贯。正是在这一点上，国际标准在维护韧性以及保持跨司法管辖区的公平竞争环境方面发挥着重要作用。

如果我们目前尚未设立巴塞尔银行监管委员会和金融稳定理事会，当前的地缘政治分裂局面也会成为创建它们的充分理由。国际标准充当着共同的基础。它们在确立最低预期的同时，为各地的本地化实施保留了灵活性。但是，避免不必要的分歧具有强有力的理由，尤其是在银行跨多个市场运营的情况下。支离破碎的监管环境可能会引发“逐底竞争”，同时增加复杂性和成本。因此，及时、全面地实施《巴塞尔协议III》仍然至关重要。

与此同时，在简化审慎框架并改善主管当局之间协调的过程中，我们必须保留有效监管的核心优势之一：识别并化解单家银行风险的能力。通用规则提供了必不可少的、基于风险的基础，而各家银行在其商业模式、治理结构、控制机制以及新兴风险敞口方面可能存在实质性差异。因此，监管机构需要有足够的空间，在必要时针对具体银行采取定性和定量措施。

这也同样适用于监管合作。我们面临的风险是全球性的——它们不会止于国界。有效应对这些风险需要主管当局之间的协调与合作。

非银行金融部门的快速增长就是一个典型例证。该部门的规模自2008年以来翻了一番，目前占欧元区金融部门资产的一半以上。然而，该部门的部分领域依然相对不透明。数据缺失和透明度有限可能导致在承压时期难以全面评估风险如何在银行与非银行机构之间传导扩散。这就是我们呼吁针对私募市场参与者提高透明度并改善信息披露的原因。我们需要国际层面的政策应对举措，以确保这些薄弱环节得到妥善处置。[10]

但是，各类风险也日益要求超出传统审慎监管当局范畴的广泛合作。

以网络韧性为例。日益复杂的基于人工智能的网络攻击的出现，正在改变网络威胁格局。先进网络能力的传播速度、规模和可获取性都在急剧上升。这就是为什么欧洲银行监管部门不仅在与银行自身紧密合作，还正在与网络安全主管机构密切协作，以增强银行应对网络风险的运营韧性。

对银行运营韧性的挑战不仅限于人工智能。量子计算已现端倪，并可能在2030年前得到广泛应用。针对密码学的量子风险已经成为现实风险，因为敏感的加密信息如今可能已被截获并存储起来，攻击者寄希望于未来技术的进步能够以“先收集、后解密”的方式将其破解。为了在这些技术演进中保持领先，监管机构越来越需要与金融领域之外的专家开展接触。

这同样适用于当前气候和自然危机带来的风险。为了更好地构建气候和自然相关风险向经济及银行资产负债表传导渠道的模型，我们正日益与包括气候科学家和生物多样性专家在内的科学界携手合作。

风险格局正在迅速演变。新技术不断涌现，现有风险在性质、规模和速度上都在发生变化，金融系统之间的互联互通也日益紧密。因此，合作绝非可有可无的额外福利，而是一种必然要求。如果我们要在维护金融稳定（两者最终所依赖的基石）的同时支持增长与竞争力，国际标准与监管合作便是不可或缺的。
有关不同司法管辖区监管风险偏好陈述的更多详情，请参见：Balan, M. 与 Zamil, R.（2026年），《在不确定性下采取行动——监管风险偏好框架的必要性》（Acting under uncertainty – the case for supervisory risk appetite frameworks），国际清算银行金融稳定学院政策实施洞见（FSI Insights on policy implementation），第74期，5月。
有关为何更广泛的韧性视角（包括治理与风险文化、运营韧性及结构性风险驱动因素）不是外围问题，而是处于审慎监管的核心，请参见：Elderson, F.（2025年），《良好监管的面貌》（What good supervision looks like），第24届金融部门政策挑战年度国际会议主旨演讲，华盛顿特区，6月12日；以及 Elderson, F.（2025年），《韧性带来竞争优势，尤其是在不确定时期》（Resilience offers a competitive advantage, especially in uncertain times），摩根士丹利欧洲金融大会主旨演讲，伦敦，3月19日。
欧盟委员会（2026年），《关于银行业竞争力与银行业单一市场的通报》（Communication on the Competitiveness of the Banking Sector and the Single Market in Banking），7月。
有关单一监管机制（SSM）简化工作的概览，请参见：Donnery, S. 与 Amis, P.（2026年），《精简监管，捍卫韧性：我们改革议程上的切实进展》（Streamlining supervision, safeguarding resilience: tangible progress on our reform agenda），欧洲央行监管博客（The Supervision Blog），7月6日。
Elderson, F.（2026年），《更简明的指引，更有效的监管》（Simpler guidance, more effective supervision），欧洲央行监管博客（The Supervision Blog），6月26日。
有关监管有效性的更多信息，请结合阅读以下演讲：Elderson, F.（2023年），《行动的权力、能力与意愿——有效银行监管的支柱》（Powers, ability and willingness to act – the mainstay of effective banking supervision），在布鲁塞尔欧元之家发表的演讲，12月7日。《良好监管的面貌》（What good supervision looks like），第24届金融部门政策挑战年度国际会议主旨演讲，华盛顿特区，6月12日。
大金融危机仍然是现代经济史上对增长最具破坏性的事件。在欧洲，以往的系统性金融危机曾导致欧盟国家蒙受平均相当于其GDP 8.5%的产出损失。参见：Lo Duca, M. 等（2017年），《欧洲国家金融危机新数据库》（A new database for financial crises in European countries），欧洲央行临时论文系列（Occasional Paper Series），第194期，7月；以及 Woods, S.（2024年），《为增长而竞争》（Competing for growth），在伦敦金融城市长官邸年度城市晚宴上的演讲，10月17日。
根据监管数据，欧元区银行的净资产收益率已大幅回升，并稳定在10%以上，达到了自单一监管机制（SSM）建立以来的最高水平区间。投资者也日益认可这一进展。与美国银行的估值差距已显著缩小，欧洲银行的平均市净率目前已接近1.5。这证明了一个重要观点：对银行而言，韧性、竞争力和盈利能力并非相互冲突的目标。
金融稳定委员会（2025年），《非银行金融中介全球监测报告》（Global Monitoring Report on Nonbank Financial Intermediation），12月16日。

topStories.title: Amazon Bedrock 扩展 Claude 模型可用性，支持在印度开展境内推理
topStories.originalTitle: Amazon Bedrock expands Claude model availability to in-country inferencing in India
topStories.source: AWS Machine Learning Blog (亚马逊云科技官方英文)
topStories.snippet: Anthropic's Claude Opus 5, Claude Sonnet 5, and Claude Haiku 4.5 are now available in India through Amazon Bedrock geographic cross-Region inference. You can access these models while processing data within the India Regions, and get started from the Amazon Bedrock console or with the Messages, InvokeModel, and Converse APIs.
topStories.fullContent:
We’re excited to announce the availability of Anthropic’s Claude Opus 5 , Claude Sonnet 5 , and Claude Haiku 4.5 in India. The India regional endpoint is served through geographic cross-Region inference . Customers in India can now access these models on Amazon Bedrock while processing the data in the India Regions in addition to the already supported global cross-Region inference . This can be useful when customers need to meet the requirements to process data locally in a desired geography.

In this post, we discuss how India geographic cross-Region inference works from the Mumbai and Hyderabad Regions on Amazon Bedrock for Anthropic Claude models. We also show how to get started from the Amazon Bedrock console and with code, using Anthropic’s Messages API, Amazon Bedrock InvokeModel API, and Converse API.

To help you achieve the scale of your AI applications, Amazon Bedrock offers cross-Region inference profiles, a feature you can use to distribute inference across multiple AWS Regions without having to manage capacity in each Region. The request originates from your source Region where you make the API call and is automatically routed to one of the destination Regions defined in the inference profile. The India geographic profile keeps inference within India. Requests route only between ap-south-1 and ap-south-2. Your input prompts and output results might move between those two Regions. Instead of being bound to the capacity of one Region, your requests draw on a broader pool of compute. This helps you maintain throughput and consistent performance under load, which matters most during traffic peaks. Cross-Region inference operates through the secure AWS network with end-to-end encryption for data in transit. Customer data is not stored in a destination Region when using cross-Region inference. It remains exclusively within the source Region. Amazon Bedrock uses a zero data retention (ZDR) data security model. This means that by default, Amazon Bedrock does not store model inputs or outputs. However, certain models require human review by AWS as a condition if content is flagged by automatic safety classifiers. For more details, see Data retention in the Amazon Bedrock User Guide. Billing and quota consumption are tracked against your account in the source Region, regardless of which backend Region handled the request. Amazon CloudWatch and AWS CloudTrail record log entries in the source Region only, so your monitoring stays in one place. Geographic cross-Region inference is available on the bedrock-runtime endpoint. It supports Anthropic’s Messages API and the native Amazon Bedrock InvokeModel and Converse APIs, along with Amazon Bedrock features such as Amazon Bedrock Guardrails and intelligent prompt routing .

Access Claude models from the Amazon Bedrock console

You can access Claude models in the text playground in the Amazon Bedrock console, which requires no coding or SDK setup. You can send prompts, adjust inference parameters, and switch between variants to get a feel for each model before you integrate the API.

Open the Amazon Bedrock console in the Region that you want to use as the source.

In the navigation pane, under Test , choose Playground .

Choose Select model in the middle of the page.

Search for Anthropic Claude Opus 5, select IN Anthropic Claude Opus 5 as the inference profile under Inference , and choose Apply .

Enter a prompt and choose Run to generate a response.

Figure 1: The Claude Opus 5 model selected in the Amazon Bedrock console playground

Call Claude models with the Anthropic Messages API and Amazon Bedrock InvokeModel and Converse API

You can access Anthropic’s Claude Opus 5, Claude Sonnet 5, or Claude Haiku 4.5 programmatically with the India geographic inference profile ID using the Anthropic Messages API on bedrock-runtime through the Anthropic SDK, or keep using the InvokeModel and Converse APIs on bedrock-runtime through the AWS Command Line Interface (AWS CLI) and AWS SDK .

Active AWS account with Amazon Bedrock access.

AWS CLI installed and configured.

Boto3 installed: pip install boto3 .

Anthropic SDK installed: pip install anthropic .

The Bedrock Token Generator for Amazon Bedrock model inference authentication installed: pip install aws_bedrock_token_generator .

AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) role or user has the necessary permissions to invoke Amazon Bedrock models using a geographic cross-Region inference profile.

Here’s a quick example using the AWS SDK for Python (Boto3) with the InvokeModel API:

import boto3 import json

# Create a Bedrock Runtime client bedrock_runtime = boto3.client( service_name="bedrock-runtime", region_name="ap-south-1" )

# Invoke Claude Sonnet 5 response = bedrock_runtime.invoke_model( modelId="in.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5", contentType="application/json", accept="application/json", body=json.dumps({ "anthropic_version": "bedrock-2023-05-31", "max_tokens": 4096, "messages": [ { "role": "user", "content": " Can you explain the features of Amazon Bedrock? " } ] }) )

result = json.loads(response["body"].read()) print(result["content"][0]["text"])

You can also use the Amazon Bedrock Converse API for a unified multi-model experience:

# Create a Bedrock Runtime client bedrock_runtime = boto3.client( service_name="bedrock-runtime", region_name="ap-south-1" )

# Invoke Claude Opus 5 response = bedrock_runtime.converse( modelId="in.anthropic.claude-opus-5", messages=[ { "role": "user", "content": [ { "text": " Can you explain the features of Amazon Bedrock?" } ] } ], inferenceConfig={ "maxTokens": 4096 } )

if 'output' in response: blocks = response['output']['message']['content'] print('\n'.join(b.get('text', '') for b in blocks if 'text' in b))

You can also use the Anthropic Messages API using the anthropic SDK package for a streamlined experience:

from anthropic import Anthropic from aws_bedrock_token_generator import provide_token

token = provide_token(region="ap-south-1")

client = Anthropic( base_url="https://bedrock-runtime.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/anthropic", api_key=token, )

response = client.messages.create( model="in. anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0", max_tokens=1024, messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Can you explain the features of Amazon Bedrock?"}], )

You can monitor usage, performance, and costs through CloudWatch and AWS Cost Explorer to scale your applications as demand grows.

With the launch of Anthropic’s Claude Opus 5, Claude Sonnet 5, and Claude Haiku 4.5 using Amazon Bedrock with India geographic cross-Region inference, you can now build highly scalable, resilient generative AI applications while keeping inference within the country. To get started, access Anthropic’s Claude models in the Amazon Bedrock console , or call them with the API using the India geographic inference profile ID. For the most current information about model availability in each Region, see Regional availability by models in the Amazon Bedrock User Guide.

Aamna is a Senior Specialist Solutions Architect for Generative AI focusing on Anthropic models and operationalizing and governing generative AI systems at scale on Amazon Bedrock. She helps ISVs solve their challenges, embrace innovation, and create new business opportunities with Amazon Bedrock.

Eugenio is a Sr. Product Marketing Manager for Amazon Bedrock at AWS. With several years of experience in generative AI, he helps customers navigate the evolving landscape of foundation models and generative AI to adopt solutions that deliver measurable value.

Sofian is a technology leader with over 12 years of experience building AI solutions, and leading high-performing teams to maximize customer outcomes. He is passionate about empowering diverse talents to drive global impact and achieve their career aspirations.

Ayan is a Principal Partner Solutions Architect and AI Tech Lead at AWS, serving as the Worldwide Tech Lead for Anthropic at AWS. He works at the intersection of cloud architecture and Artificial Intelligence, helping organizations adopt and scale Anthropic’s technologies on AWS.
topStories.fullTranslation:
我们很高兴地宣布，Anthropic 的 Claude Opus 5、Claude Sonnet 5 和 Claude Haiku 4.5 现已在印度上线。印度区域终端节点通过地理跨区域推理提供服务。除了已支持的全球跨区域推理之外，印度客户现在可以在 Amazon Bedrock 上访问这些模型，并在印度各区域内处理数据。这有助于满足客户在特定地理区域内进行本地数据处理的合规要求。

在本文中，我们将讨论印度地理跨区域推理在 Amazon Bedrock 上针对孟买和海得拉巴区域的 Anthropic Claude 模型是如何运作的。我们还将展示如何通过 Amazon Bedrock 控制台以及借助代码（使用 Anthropic 的 Messages API、Amazon Bedrock InvokeModel API 和 Converse API）快速上手。

为了帮助您实现 AI 应用程序的规模化扩展，Amazon Bedrock 提供了跨区域推理配置文件（cross-Region inference profiles），您可以使用该功能将推理任务分发到多个 AWS 区域，而无需在每个区域分别管理算力配额。请求始于您发起 API 调用的源区域，并自动路由到推理配置文件中定义的目标区域之一。印度地理配置文件将推理限制在印度境内。请求仅在 ap-south-1（孟买）和 ap-south-2（海得拉巴）之间路由。您的输入提示词和输出结果可能会在这两个区域之间流动。您的请求不再受限于单一区域的容量，而是可以利用更广泛的计算资源池。这有助于您在负载下保持吞吐量和一致的性能，这在流量高峰期间至关重要。跨区域推理通过安全的 AWS 网络运行，传输中的数据具有端到端加密保护。使用跨区域推理时，客户数据不会存储在目标区域，而是仅保留在源区域内。Amazon Bedrock 采用零数据保留（ZDR）数据安全模型。这意味着在默认情况下，Amazon Bedrock 不会存储模型输入或输出。不过，如果内容被自动化安全分类器标记，某些模型会要求 AWS 进行人工复核作为条件。有关更多详细信息，请参阅《Amazon Bedrock 用户指南》中的“数据保留”部分。无论由哪个后端区域处理请求，计费和配额消耗都会记在您源区域的账户下。Amazon CloudWatch 和 AWS CloudTrail 仅在源区域记录日志条目，因此您的监控保留在一个统一的位置。地理跨区域推理在 bedrock-runtime 终端节点上可用。它支持 Anthropic 的 Messages API 以及原生的 Amazon Bedrock InvokeModel 和 Converse API，同时还支持 Amazon Bedrock 的各项功能，例如 Amazon Bedrock Guardrails 和智能提示词路由。

通过 Amazon Bedrock 控制台访问 Claude 模型
您可以在 Amazon Bedrock 控制台的文本演练场（playground）中访问 Claude 模型，该方式无需编写代码或配置 SDK。在集成 API 之前，您可以发送提示词、调整推理参数并在各变体之间切换，以体验每个模型的表现。

在您希望用作源区域的区域中打开 Amazon Bedrock 控制台。
在导航窗格中的“Test”（测试）下，选择“Playground”（演练场）。
选择页面中间的“Select model”（选择模型）。
搜索 Anthropic Claude Opus 5，在“Inference”（推理）下选择“IN Anthropic Claude Opus 5”作为推理配置文件，然后选择“Apply”（应用）。
输入提示词并选择“Run”（运行）以生成响应。
图 1：在 Amazon Bedrock 控制台演练场中选择 Claude Opus 5 模型

使用 Anthropic Messages API 以及 Amazon Bedrock InvokeModel 和 Converse API 调用 Claude 模型
您可以使用印度地理推理配置文件 ID，通过 Anthropic SDK 在 bedrock-runtime 上使用 Anthropic Messages API 以编程方式访问 Anthropic 的 Claude Opus 5、Claude Sonnet 5 或 Claude Haiku 4.5；或者通过 AWS 命令行界面（AWS CLI）和 AWS SDK，继续在 bedrock-runtime 上使用 InvokeModel 和 Converse API。

具有 Amazon Bedrock 访问权限的有效 AWS 账户。
已安装并配置 AWS CLI。
已安装 Boto3：pip install boto3。
已安装 Anthropic SDK：pip install anthropic。
已安装用于 Amazon Bedrock 模型推理身份验证的 Bedrock Token Generator：pip install aws_bedrock_token_generator。
AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) 角色或用户具有使用地理跨区域推理配置文件调用 Amazon Bedrock 模型的必要权限。

以下是使用适用于 Python 的 AWS SDK (Boto3) 配合 InvokeModel API 的快速示例：
import boto3 import json
# 创建 Bedrock Runtime 客户端
bedrock_runtime = boto3.client( service_name="bedrock-runtime", region_name="ap-south-1" )
# 调用 Claude Sonnet 5
response = bedrock_runtime.invoke_model( modelId="in.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5", contentType="application/json", accept="application/json", body=json.dumps({ "anthropic_version": "bedrock-2023-05-31", "max_tokens": 4096, "messages": [ { "role": "user", "content": " Can you explain the features of Amazon Bedrock? " } ] }) )
result = json.loads(response["body"].read())
print(result["content"][0]["text"])

您也可以使用 Amazon Bedrock Converse API 获得统一的多模型体验：
# 创建 Bedrock Runtime 客户端
bedrock_runtime = boto3.client( service_name="bedrock-runtime", region_name="ap-south-1" )
# 调用 Claude Opus 5
response = bedrock_runtime.converse( modelId="in.anthropic.claude-opus-5", messages=[ { "role": "user", "content": [ { "text": " Can you explain the features of Amazon Bedrock?" } ] } ], inferenceConfig={ "maxTokens": 4096 } )
if 'output' in response:
    blocks = response['output']['message']['content']
    print('\n'.join(b.get('text', '') for b in blocks if 'text' in b))

您还可以通过 anthropic SDK 包使用 Anthropic Messages API 以获得精简的使用体验：
from anthropic import Anthropic from aws_bedrock_token_generator import provide_token
token = provide_token(region="ap-south-1")

topStories.originalTitle: Introducing Anthropic models on Amazon Bedrock for in-region inference in Seoul and Singapore
topStories.source: AWS Machine Learning Blog (亚马逊云科技官方英文)
topStories.snippet: Amazon Bedrock now supports Anthropic's Claude Opus 5 and Claude Sonnet 5 with in-region inference in Seoul, and Claude Sonnet 5 in Singapore. If you have local data processing requirements in South Korea or Singapore, you can now use these Anthropic models at scale, with inference processed entirely within the Region you call.
topStories.fullContent:
Amazon Bedrock now supports the Anthropic Claude models: Claude Opus 5 and Claude Sonnet 5 in Seoul and Claude Sonnet 5 in Singapore with in-region inference on the bedrock-runtime endpoint. If you have local data processing requirements in South Korea or Singapore, for example, in financial services, healthcare, and the public sector, you can now use these Anthropic models at scale. Amazon Bedrock processes inference requests and data within the Region you call. The processing does not leave the Region.

In this post, we walk through how in-region inference works from the Asia Pacific (Seoul) Region ( ap-northeast-2 ) and Asia Pacific (Singapore) Region ( ap-southeast-1 ) using the bedrock-runtime endpoint. We also show how to get started from the Amazon Bedrock console and with code, using the Amazon Bedrock Converse API, the InvokeModel API, and the Anthropic Messages API.

To help you meet strict data residency requirements for your AI applications, Amazon Bedrock offers in-region inference. Your request is processed entirely within the single AWS Region you specify, and it does not leave that Region. Use this when you have a need for strict single-Region data processing.

Unlike cross-Region inference profiles, there is no routing layer. The request you send to the Seoul ( ap-northeast-2 ) or Singapore ( ap-southeast-1 ) Region is served by that Region alone. Your input prompts and output results stay within it for the full lifecycle of the request. In exchange, your throughput is bounded by that Region’s capacity. Requests are subject to per-Region service quotas. Billing follows standard on-demand pricing for the Region you call. Quota consumption, Amazon CloudWatch metrics, and AWS CloudTrail log entries are all scoped to that same Region. There is no source-versus-destination distinction to account for in your monitoring. In-region inference for Claude Sonnet 5 and Claude Opus 5 in Seoul and Claude Sonnet 5 in Singapore is available on the bedrock-runtime endpoint. For new applications, we recommend the bedrock-runtime endpoint. You invoke it with the direct model ID, for example, anthropic.claude-opus-5 or anthropic.claude-sonnet-5 . It supports Anthropic’s Messages API and the Amazon Bedrock InvokeModel and Converse APIs, along with Amazon Bedrock features such as Amazon Bedrock Guardrails and intelligent prompt routing .

Access Claude models from the Amazon Bedrock console

You can access Claude models in the text playground in the Amazon Bedrock console, which requires no coding or SDK setup. You can send prompts, adjust inference parameters, and switch between variants to get a feel for each model before you integrate the API.

Open the Amazon Bedrock console in a Region that you want to use as a source.

In the navigation pane, under Test , choose Playground .

Choose Select model in the middle of the page.

Search for anthropic.claude-opus-5 , select On-Demand under Inference , and choose Apply .

Enter a prompt and choose Run to generate a response.

Figure 1: The Anthropic Opus 5 model selected in the Amazon Bedrock console playground with in-region inference

Call Claude models with the Anthropic Messages API and Amazon Bedrock InvokeModel and Converse API

You can access Anthropic’s Claude Opus 5 or Claude Sonnet 5 programmatically with Seoul in-region inference using the Anthropic Messages API on the bedrock-runtime through Anthropic SDK or keep using the Invoke and Converse API on bedrock-runtime through the AWS Command Line Interface (AWS CLI) and AWS SDK .

Active AWS account with Amazon Bedrock access.

AWS CLI installed and configured.

Boto3 installed: pip install boto3 .

Anthropic SDK installed: pip install anthropic .

The Amazon Bedrock Token Generator for Amazon Bedrock authentication installed: pip install aws_bedrock_token_generator .

Here’s a quick example using the AWS SDK for Python (Boto3) with the InvokeModel API:

import boto3 import json

# Create a Bedrock Runtime client with in-region inference in Singapore bedrock_runtime = boto3.client( service_name="bedrock-runtime", region_name="ap-southeast-1")

# Invoke Claude Sonnet 5 response = bedrock_runtime.invoke_model( modelId="anthropic.claude-sonnet-5", contentType="application/json", accept="application/json", body=json.dumps({ "anthropic_version": "bedrock-2023-05-31", "max_tokens": 4096, "messages": [ { "role": "user", "content": " Can you explain the features of Amazon Bedrock? " } ] }) )

result = json.loads(response["body"].read()) print(result["content"][0]["text"])

You can also use the Amazon Bedrock Converse API for a unified multi-model experience:

# Create a Bedrock Runtime client with in-region inference in Seoul bedrock_runtime = boto3.client( service_name="bedrock-runtime", region_name="ap-northeast-2" )

# Invoke Claude Opus 5 response = bedrock_runtime.converse( modelId="anthropic.claude-opus-5", messages=[ { "role": "user", "content": [ { "text": " Can you explain the features of Amazon Bedrock?" } ] } ], inferenceConfig={ "maxTokens": 4096 } )

if 'output' in response: blocks = response['output']['message']['content'] print('\n'.join(b.get('text', '') for b in blocks if 'text' in b))

You can also use the Anthropic Messages API through the anthropic SDK package for a streamlined experience:

from anthropic import Anthropic from aws_bedrock_token_generator import provide_token

token = provide_token(region="ap-northeast-2")

client = Anthropic( base_url="https://bedrock-runtime.ap-northeast-2.amazonaws.com/anthropic", api_key=token, )

response = client.messages.create( model="anthropic.claude-sonnet-5", max_tokens=1024, messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Can you explain the features of Amazon Bedrock?"}], )

You can monitor usage, performance, and costs through CloudWatch and AWS Cost Explorer to scale your applications as demand grows.

With the launch of Anthropic’s Claude Opus 5 and Claude Sonnet 5 on Amazon Bedrock with in-region inference in Seoul, and Claude Sonnet 5 with in-region inference in Singapore, you can now build generative AI applications that have strict data residency requirements. This keeps inference within the Region you want. We are excited about this launch and look forward to seeing how you use these capabilities to accelerate innovation and deliver impactful AI-powered experiences across the Region. For the most current information about model availability in each Region, see Regional availability by models in the Amazon Bedrock User Guide.

Aamna is a Senior Specialist Solutions Architect for Generative AI focusing on Anthropic models and operationalizing and governing generative AI systems at scale on Amazon Bedrock. She helps ISVs solve their challenges, embrace innovation, and create new business opportunities with Amazon Bedrock.

Alfredo is a Senior Specialist Solutions Architect for Generative AI at AWS, focusing on Anthropic models go-to-market on Amazon Bedrock. He works with Financial Services customers to design and scale generative AI solutions across distributed systems and turn generative AI experiments into production workloads. Outside of work, he is passionate about family and endurance sports.

Eugenio is a Sr. Product Marketing Manager for Amazon Bedrock at AWS. With several years of experience in generative AI, he helps customers navigate the evolving landscape of foundation models and generative AI to adopt solutions that deliver measurable value.

Sofian is a technology leader with over 12 years of experience building AI solutions, and leading high-performing teams to maximize customer outcomes. He is passionate about empowering diverse talents to drive global impact and achieve their career aspirations.

Amazon Bedrock 现已支持 Anthropic Claude 模型：首尔区域支持 Claude Opus 5 和 Claude Sonnet 5，新加坡区域支持 Claude Sonnet 5，均通过 bedrock-runtime 终端节点提供区域内推理（in-region inference）。如果您在韩国或新加坡有本地数据处理合规要求（例如在金融服务、医疗保健以及公共部门），现在便可以大规模使用这些 Anthropic 模型。Amazon Bedrock 会完全在您调用的区域内处理推理请求和数据，数据处理绝不会离开该区域。

在本文中，我们将介绍如何通过 bedrock-runtime 终端节点，在亚太地区（首尔）区域（ap-northeast-2）和亚太地区（新加坡）区域（ap-southeast-1）使用区域内推理。我们还将展示如何通过 Amazon Bedrock 控制台以及使用 Amazon Bedrock Converse API、InvokeModel API 和 Anthropic Messages API 编写代码开始上手。

为了帮助您满足 AI 应用程序严格的数据驻留（data residency）要求，Amazon Bedrock 提供了区域内推理。您的请求将完全在您指定的单个 AWS 区域内处理，且不会离开该区域。当您对严格的单区域数据处理有需求时，请使用此模式。

与跨区域推理配置文件（cross-Region inference profiles）不同，此模式没有路由层。您发送到首尔（ap-northeast-2）或新加坡（ap-southeast-1）区域的请求仅由该区域独立处理。在请求的整个生命周期中，您的输入提示词和输出结果都会保留在该区域内。作为交换，您的吞吐量受限于该区域的容量。请求受各区域服务配额的约束。计费遵循您所调用区域的标准按需定价。配额消耗、Amazon CloudWatch 指标和 AWS CloudTrail 日志条目均局限于同一区域。在监控中无需区分源区域与目标区域。首尔的 Claude Sonnet 5、Claude Opus 5 以及新加坡的 Claude Sonnet 5 的区域内推理可在 bedrock-runtime 终端节点上使用。对于新应用程序，我们推荐使用 bedrock-runtime 终端节点。您可以使用直接的模型 ID 调用它，例如 anthropic.claude-opus-5 或 anthropic.claude-sonnet-5。它支持 Anthropic 的 Messages API 以及 Amazon Bedrock 的 InvokeModel 和 Converse API，同时还支持 Amazon Bedrock 的各项功能，例如 Amazon Bedrock Guardrails 和智能提示词路由（intelligent prompt routing）。

从 Amazon Bedrock 控制台访问 Claude 模型
您可以在 Amazon Bedrock 控制台的文本演练场（Playground）中访问 Claude 模型，该操作无需编码或配置 SDK。在集成 API 之前，您可以发送提示词、调整推理参数并在各变体之间切换，以体验各个模型的性能表现。

在要用作源的区域中打开 Amazon Bedrock 控制台。
在导航窗格的“Test”（测试）下，选择“Playground”（演练场）。
在页面中间选择“Select model”（选择模型）。
搜索 anthropic.claude-opus-5，在“Inference”（推理）下选择“On-Demand”（按需），然后选择“Apply”（应用）。
输入提示词并选择“Run”（运行）以生成响应。

图 1：在 Amazon Bedrock 控制台演练场中选定采用区域内推理的 Anthropic Opus 5 模型

使用 Anthropic Messages API 以及 Amazon Bedrock InvokeModel 和 Converse API 调用 Claude 模型
您可以通过 Anthropic SDK 在 bedrock-runtime 上使用 Anthropic Messages API 以编程方式访问 Anthropic 的 Claude Opus 5 或 Claude Sonnet 5 进行首尔区域内推理，也可以继续通过 AWS 命令行界面（AWS CLI）和 AWS SDK 在 bedrock-runtime 上使用 Invoke 和 Converse API。

具备 Amazon Bedrock 访问权限的有效 AWS 账户。
已安装并配置 AWS CLI。
已安装 Boto3：pip install boto3。
已安装 Anthropic SDK：pip install anthropic。
已安装用于 Amazon Bedrock 身份验证的 Amazon Bedrock Token Generator：pip install aws_bedrock_token_generator。

以下是结合 InvokeModel API 使用适用于 Python 的 AWS SDK（Boto3）的简要示例：
import boto3 import json
# 创建在新加坡具备区域内推理能力的 Bedrock Runtime 客户端
bedrock_runtime = boto3.client( service_name="bedrock-runtime", region_name="ap-southeast-1")
# 调用 Claude Sonnet 5
response = bedrock_runtime.invoke_model( modelId="anthropic.claude-sonnet-5", contentType="application/json", accept="application/json", body=json.dumps({ "anthropic_version": "bedrock-2023-05-31", "max_tokens": 4096, "messages": [ { "role": "user", "content": " Can you explain the features of Amazon Bedrock? " } ] }) )
result = json.loads(response["body"].read())
print(result["content"][0]["text"])

您也可以使用 Amazon Bedrock Converse API 获得统一的多模型体验：
# 创建在首尔具备区域内推理能力的 Bedrock Runtime 客户端
bedrock_runtime = boto3.client( service_name="bedrock-runtime", region_name="ap-northeast-2" )
# 调用 Claude Opus 5
response = bedrock_runtime.converse( modelId="anthropic.claude-opus-5", messages=[ { "role": "user", "content": [ { "text": " Can you explain the features of Amazon Bedrock?" } ] } ], inferenceConfig={ "maxTokens": 4096 } )
if 'output' in response:
    blocks = response['output']['message']['content']
    print('\n'.join(b.get('text', '') for b in blocks if 'text' in b))

token = provide_token(region="ap-northeast-2")
client = Anthropic( base_url="https://bedrock-runtime.ap-northeast-2.amazonaws.com/anthropic", api_key=token, )
response = client.messages.create( model="anthropic.claude-sonnet-5", max_tokens=1024, messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Can you explain the features of Amazon Bedrock?"}], )

您可以随着业务需求的增长，通过 CloudWatch 和 AWS Cost Explorer 监控使用量、性能和成本，以扩展应用程序规模。

随着 Anthropic 的 Claude Opus 5 和 Claude Sonnet 5 在 Amazon Bedrock 首尔区域内推理上线，以及 Claude Sonnet 5 在新加坡区域内推理上线，您现在可以构建满足严格数据驻留要求的生成式 AI 应用程序。这使推理始终保留在您所需的区域内。我们对此次发布倍感振奋，并期待看到您如何利用这些功能加速创新，在全区域范围内提供具有影响力的 AI 驱动体验。有关各区域模型可用性的最新信息，请参阅《Amazon Bedrock 用户指南》中的“按模型划分的区域可用性”。
