trendStories.fullTranslation:
上周我发表了《那 Rails 怎么办？》（What About Rails），深入探讨了 DHH 在 Rails World 上的主题演讲。比我聪明的人对此发表了有趣的看法：

“你拥有了有史以来最强大的工具，你已经成为了千倍创造者（1000x maker），难道你就想不到如何让你的技术栈提升 10 倍吗？”

何塞·瓦利姆（José Valim）提出了一个绝佳的问题。我试图去寻找答案。

“它们很快就不会再是 Web 应用了。它们将成为原生应用，因为开发这些东西的成本几乎降到了零。”

前端转向原生应用、后端转向 Rust，并非关乎某项特定的技术，而是关乎成本。DHH 并不是第一个提出这一论点的人。

早在八月份，丹·卢（Dan Luu）就发表了《软件再也没有慢的借口了》（There’s no reason for software to be slow anymore）。在文中，他辩称专门的性能优化工作成本大幅下降（因为大语言模型 LLM），以至于现在几乎任何人都能负担得起。

卢比 DHH 谨慎得多。他指出，智能体（agent）会在基准测试中过拟合，在缺乏人类协助时很不擅长实验设计，而且获得严谨结果所需的时间并没有减少，减少的只是获得一个看似有趣的结果所需的时间。

不久之后，瓦伦·甘地（Varun Gandhi）发表了自己的回应，题为《软件仍然有慢下去的理由》（There continue to be reasons for software to be slow）。他指出了这种论点的形式逻辑：做 X 的成本太高，LLM 将成本除以了一个庞大的数字，因此人们现在就会去做 X。甘地认为，虽然这对像卢这样的人（从事自己项目的专家）确实成立，但那些情况十分罕见。

把 X 替换为 Rust 后端、六款原生应用，或者上周五前赶出的 CLI，你就能得到 DHH 主题演讲的推介辞。DHH 是一位在他自己控股的公司里从事自己产品的专家。甘地指出，这正是最有可能奏效的情境。这里甚至没有经理来卡预算。如果它在任何地方能起效，那就是在这里。他把一个最理想状态下的结果，泛化成了“到 12 月时，几乎所有程序员、几乎所有公司都将如此”。

甘地最有价值的见解在于，编写代码1从来都不是最主要的成本。我们还必须考虑发布变更、维护它们以及避免回归缺陷。DHH 对 Hey Next 的体验不过才一周时间，它甚至都还不是一个生产系统。

他自己就向我们展示了这一点。Basecamp 5 的“瑞士奶酪”架构，正是脱胎于“代码很便宜，但协调成本却不菲”这一现实。甘地讲述了同一个故事的另一个版本：Bun 借助 LLM 辅助对 Zig 进行了分支（fork），编译速度提升了 4 倍，但却无法合并回上游，因为没有人2想要一个结果不确定的编译器。

消除一个瓶颈并不能消除排队现象；它只会向你揭示下一个制约因素在哪里。有了 LLM，我们只是将瓶颈向右移动了一步，从编写代码移到了之后发生的一切事务上。而 DHH 的解决方案就是跳过这些事务。

“现在，部分原因在于像 Rust 这样的编程语言极度冗长，对人类来说毫无观赏性。所以我不去看它，我允许智能体直接吐出超出必要的内容，这种方式在我的 Ruby 代码中我是绝不会容忍的。”

甘地认为成本论点失效的原因之一是，人们的容忍度提高了。当工作变成异步且由智能体驱动时，我们不再面对面地承受变慢的 git、更迟钝的自动补全和更漫长的构建过程。没有人在那里干等着。如果你仍然在意这些事情，你大概会讨厌这一点。

而 DHH 把这一切都跳过了。你把任务交代出去，“就像对待同事一样”，然后“等有东西准备好了再回去审查”。这里的“审查”并不意味着代码审查；它意味着检查那个按钮是否能用。

也许对于他个人的一次性项目来说这没问题。从 Hey Next 启动一周来看，这似乎行得通。但他自身容忍度的提高并不会提高其他人的容忍度。他可以不去在乎 Hey Next 这个黑盒子里装了什么，但很多人在乎 Rails 盒子里装了什么。所谓的“几乎所有程序员”到头来也不过如此。

所以，回到瓦利姆的问题。你拥有无限的 Token。你是一个千倍创造者。你可以创造任何东西。难道你就找不出任何东西，哪怕任何一件能为 Rails 创造的东西吗？

这从来都不是预算的问题。速度的提升并不会改变优先级。DHH 今年打造的一切，都是他自己想要的。他正在构建的东西没有一样需要 Rails 变得更好，所以他也未曾让它变得更好。

我们现在可以想要一切。我们现在可以得到一切。

那么，这“一切”究竟是什么？事实证明，是一个计算器。一个视频编辑器。一些演示文稿软件。又一个 Linux 发行版。以及对他自己产品的一次重写。他被赋予了无限的 Token，而这就是他所能构想出的全部。这里确实存在匮乏。思想的匮乏。

看看那个清单吧。没有一个全新的点子。这是当下整个行业的缩影。DHH 的欲望展露无遗，他想要的无非属于他自己的东西，以及早已存在的东西。

LLM 极其擅长制造早已存在的东西。卢承认这一点；早期的模型甚至过拟合到了滑稽的地步3。要求做一个计算器是个稳妥的诉求。而在 2004 年，Rails 绝非稳妥之物。它是新颖的，并因此备受赞誉。

DHH 的主题演讲本末倒置了。手写代码的时代并不是某种我们已经超越的温情旧梦。在 LLM 出现之前，将一个想法付诸实践需要付出多得多的跑腿苦工。但你首先需要灵感的火花，而你现在依然需要它。

在 2005 年，“看看我没有去做的所有事情”是一种自豪的夸耀。今年他重演了这一幕以作类比。但在我看来，他如今不再去做的那件事，恰恰是提出新的想法。

1 “编写”包含设计与调试，而不仅仅是打字。↩
2 嗯，除了 Bun，他们的分支只要对他们自己管用就行。↩
3 延伸阅读：西奈山医院研究发现，人工智能和人类一样会妄下结论 ↩

让我们探讨一下如何结合工厂方法模式使用数据和值对象，以帮助解耦软件组件。
我为 Ruby 做了一个 Web 框架。好吧，其实并没有。但差不多算吧。

trendStories.title: Deser：重新思考 Rust 的序列化机制
trendStories.fullContent:
written on September 29, 2026

Serde is an amazing serialization library for Rust and it has been a huge reason why I felt productive with it for years. However already while at Sentry I got quite frustrated with some of the limitations with it but actually replacing Serde is tricky because of the might that it has in the ecosystem. Also because it’s quite hard to actually do better without also making some potentially painful compromises.

Here are three examples of Serde corner cases that show poor interactions of Serde features or unexpected limitations:

An internally tagged enum, with serde_json‘s arbitrary_precision feature turned on:

Serde’s data model has no place for arbitrary precision numbers, so serde_json uses in-band signalling with a map with a magic key. The enum has to buffer the fields until it has seen the tag, and the buffer does not know about the magic key. Because Cargo features are unified, it’s enough for any crate in your dependency graph to turn the feature on.

Stats on its own parses {"scores": {"42": 23}} just fine. JSON keys are always strings, and serde_json only turns them into integers if the type asks for one. However once flatten buffers the value, "42" is just a string. The error also points at the end of the document rather than at the key.

A function cannot be passed as a type parameter, so there is no way to apply from_hex to the inside of an Option, a Vec or a map. You write another function for every wrapper, and once you have from_opt_hex the field is no longer optional unless you also remember to add #[serde(default)].

None of these are bugs that are easy to fix in Serde. They fall out of its design, and that design is protected by Serde’s stability guarantees.

Back in 2022 I started an experiment called Deser. It’s a serialization library for Rust that takes the user experience of Serde and puts it on top of a completely different architecture inspired by miniserde. I never really finished it and it sat around for a few years. I picked it back up, and it has now reached a point where I think it’s worth looking at. Even just to inspire others to see if they want to explore the space.

The name is Serde with its two halves swapped. Deser is Serde but the other way around. In Serde, a type drives the deserialization process: a Deserialize impl asks the deserializer for the kind of value it expects, the format calls back into a visitor. Every nested value is handled by recursion which makes Serde deserialization inherently grow the stack with each level of nesting.

Deser on the other hand turns this around and the format tells the type of the next value and pushes events into a sink. When a sink hits the start of a nested value, it doesn’t call into it but hands back a new sink to a driver, which keeps all state on the heap (in fact, in an arena). On the way out, emitters return their nested values instead of recursing into them.

That also means that Deser cannot support formats like protobuf that are not self describing. They are in fact quite intentionally left out of the design entirely. Which is one way to say: if you want to “fix” Serde, you need to make some other compromises.

Most of the reasons for Deser’s ideas go back to Sentry Relay, which processes enormous amounts of untrusted JSON. Over the years when I was at Sentry we ran into the same set of problems again and again, and many of them are not really bugs in Serde but consequences of its design. Serde’s stability guarantees mean that a lot of them cannot be fixed without breaking every format and every hand written implementation. Most of these problems come from three decisions:

One set of traits for all formats. Serde serves both self describing formats (JSON, YAML, TOML, …) and formats where the reader has to know the type upfront (postcard, bincode, protobuf, …). That is incredibly useful, but it means that some features only work with some formats, and you find out at runtime. In case of Serde it also has some odd wrinkles where a derived struct quietly accepts an array in place of an object in JSON for instance.

A fixed data model that loses information when buffering. Internally tagged enums, untagged enums and flatten need to buffer values before they know what to do with them. The buffer can’t hold everything the format knew, errors lose their location and extensions to the ecosystem rely on in-band signalling to express things such as arbitrary precision numbers.

Recursion on the call stack. Every level of nesting uses stack space. Formats protect against this with a recursion limit, but the moment you go through a code path that doesn’t have one (writing, dynamic values), deeply nested data can take down your process. It also means that a deserialization cannot be paused while you wait for more input.

Many of the corresponding Serde issues have been open for years, and I wrote about abusing Serde before. People have tried different angles on this over the years. Some went minimal and dropped most features to get fast compiles and no recursion. dtolnay’s own miniserde is the best example of that, and deser’s trait design was originally modelled after it. Other recent attempts went for runtime reflection, or for a new data model with a focus on binary formats.

If you want to read up on all of the collected challenges with Serde’s design, I maintain a lengthy list here.

First of all I don’t think it’s likely that one can replace Serde. The orphan rule entrenches Serde incredibly well in the ecosystem. But some things are within the reach of a crate author’s control. In case of Deser it’s completeness.

Deser today implements all important self describing formats from YAML, JSON, TOML, CBOR, JSON5 and the likes, but also XML and plist to really close the gap. XML in particular is something Serde has declined to support, and it shows (more on that below). At the very least format support should not be the reason not to use Deser.

The second problem usually is that actually solving Serde’s issues comes at a significant cost in compile time and/or runtime performance. Deser is no different. While Deser’s compile times are a bit better than Serde’s, the binary bloat is quite a bit worse and the runtime performance is mixed. It’s roughly comparable if you look at the numbers but depending on the format structure you are losing significantly from some of the tradeoffs.

That said, it’s now in a state where it’s at least in principle a drop-in replacement where the tradeoffs might work well for users.

Deser does not try to be significantly different than Serde on the surface level. For most uses you derive Serialize and Deserialize and then start using it with your format implementing crate of choice. Most attributes are very similar, though they are taking Rust expressions instead of strings.

The difference in the design would become more apparent if you implement a serializer or deserializer yourself. Instead of visitors that call into each other recursively, deserializing a type creates a sink which receives events that are directly emitted by the parser, and serializing produces emitters that hand out values. Nested sinks and emitters are handed back to a driver, which keeps them on the heap. This design, which is entirely stolen from miniserde, gives some interesting consequences:

On top of that are a lot of things that I just wanted to have:

Here is a small configuration type that shows a few of these together:

Adapters are types, so Hex can go inside a Vec, and DisplayFromStr inside a Vec inside an Option. Validators are adapters too, so Check<NonEmpty, Vec<Hex>> decodes the keys and then checks that there is at least one. The catch-all variant keeps the tag and a recording of everything else in case someone wants to process it later.

Errors are something I care a lot about, so here is what happens when a value is wrong:

Note that here the tag of the internally tagged enum comes last which means that the values have to be buffered until the tag is known. In Serde this is tricky and we would lose the location if we used some tricks to add it. With Deser however, with the path layer enabled Deser you where in the structure the problem is:

Deser really wants to be extensible, and XML is a more extreme example of the differences between Deser and Serde. Here is an Atom entry that mixes in Dublin Core for the authors:

XML uses namespaces which means that names need to be matched by their namespace, not by the prefix the document happens to use. Here the document says d: and the type says dc!. atom!("title") is just the string {http://www.w3.org/2005/Atom}title, which works because attributes are expressions. The two creators are collected into one Vec even though there is another element between them, and the text of updated goes straight into a chrono datetime. Because the enum is untagged, the entry has to be buffered before a variant is picked, and deser’s buffer keeps both creators. So the result is an Entry with John and Jane.

quick-xml, the most popular XML crate for Serde, drops the prefixes and ignores namespaces entirely, so a <x:title> from some other namespace is happily accepted as the title of the entry. The split list part though is considerably worse. A plain Entry fails with a duplicate field error for creator, unless you turn on the overlapped-lists feature (which, remember, is a global additive flag that any crate could set). That feature makes quick-xml read ahead to the end of the element and buffer everything in between, without a limit unless you set one.

But the feature only helps when quick-xml is hooked up to the struct directly and no buffering is taking place. Wrap the struct in the untagged enum and Serde buffers the entry itself. Read from that buffer, Entry sees creator twice and fails again. The fallback is a map, which keeps only the last creator, and there is no error. With or without the feature you get this:

Notice how John is gone.

Format specific extension types such as TOML datetimes are another case. TOML has them natively, Serde’s data model does not, so the toml crate passes them on as a map with a magic key. In Deser a datetime is an extension value, which formats that know it keep and all others write as a string:

The same with serde_json::Value gives you {"released":{"$__toml_private_datetime":"2026-09-29T21:00:00+02:00"}}, and reading the value into a chrono::DateTime fails outright with invalid type: map, expected an RFC 3339 formatted date and time string.

So now that you know Deser is at least in theory cool, at what cost?

It is not free. The design relies on dynamic dispatch and on sinks and emitters that live on the heap, and that has considerable runtime overhead. In my own measurements for JSON, Deser reads somewhere between 33% faster and 60% slower than serde_json depending on the data. On average it’s about 10% slower for reading. Writes are between three times as fast and 70% slower and a wash on average. For YAML and TOML it’s noticeably faster than the Serde based crates, but that is more about the format implementations than the architecture.

Compile times slightly are better, but not dramatically so. Because it doesn’t monomorphize everything, release builds of derived code are about 2.3 times as fast as with Serde and that get a tiny bit better in practice for your own code as less recompilation is necessary.

To make Deser’s design work at all, it also uses unsafe internally. Most of this is to keep the chain of borrowed sinks on the heap. I feel like this is fine in the days of Miri and agents, but I know it makes some folks uneasy.

And well, the biggest cost is that it’s just not Serde.

Quite a lot actually which might be surprising. In addition to the core there is support for derive.

It supports all flavorts of JSON you can think of: JSON, JSONC, JSON5 and HJSON. (Fun fact here: they are all generated out of one shared parser template) For binary handling it supports CBOR and MessagePack. Additionally it does YAML 1.1 and 1.2, TOML, XML and all three flavors of Apple’s plist as well as CSV/TSV, urlencoded data and environment variables. For more crazy contraptions you can attach path info or capture location data as well as support for debug printing. You can perform validation as you parse, opt into different binary encodings in addition to base64, you can bridge to serde or capture dynamic values, transcode between formats or hook it up with tokio.

For documentation see docs.rs/deser and the code itself is on GitHub alongside many examples.

trendStories.fullTranslation:
写于 2026 年 9 月 29 日
Serde 是一款令人惊艳的 Rust 序列化库，多年来它一直是我在 Rust 中保持高生产力的重要原因。然而，早在 Sentry 工作时，我就对其存在的某些局限感到十分沮丧；但真正去取代 Serde 却非常棘手，因为它在整个生态中具有极其强大的影响力。此外，如果不做出一些可能相当痛苦的妥协，实际上也很难做得更好。
以下是 Serde 边界情况的三个例子，展示了 Serde 特性之间不佳的交互或是意料之外的限制：
一个内部带标签的枚举（internally tagged enum），且开启了 serde_json 的 arbitrary_precision 特性：
Serde 的数据模型没有容纳任意精度数字的位置，因此 serde_json 采用了带魔法键的映射（map）来进行带内信令（in-band signalling）。该枚举必须先缓冲字段，直到看到标签为止，而缓冲区并不知道这个魔法键的存在。由于 Cargo 的特性是统一合并的（unified），只要你的依赖图中有任何一个 crate 开启了该特性，就会触发此问题。
Stats 本身可以顺利解析 {"scores": {"42": 23}}。JSON 的键始终是字符串，serde_json 仅在类型要求时才会将它们转换为整数。然而，一旦 flatten 缓冲了该值，"42" 就仅仅只是一个字符串了。而且报错位置指向的是文档末尾，而不是那个键。
函数不能作为类型参数传递，因此无法将 from_hex 应用到 Option、Vec 或 map 的内部。你必须为每个包装器另外编写一个函数，而一旦你有了 from_opt_hex，该字段就不再是可选的了，除非你还记得加上 #[serde(default)]。
这些都不是在 Serde 中容易修复的 bug。它们源于其整体架构设计，而这一设计又受到 Serde 稳定性保证的保护。
早在 2022 年，我启动了一个名为 Deser 的实验项目。它是一个 Rust 序列化库，继承了 Serde 的用户体验，并将其置于受 miniserde 启发的完全不同的架构之上。我当时并没有真正完成它，它就这样搁置了几年。最近我重新拾起了它，现在它已经发展到了我认为值得一看的阶段。哪怕仅仅是为了启发其他人，看看是否有人想探索这个领域。
它的名字就是把 Serde 的前后两半调换了一下。Deser 本质上就是反过来的 Serde。在 Serde 中，由类型来驱动反序列化过程：Deserialize 的实现会向反序列化器询问它所期望的值类型，数据格式再回调访问器（visitor）。每个嵌套值都通过递归来处理，这使得 Serde 的反序列化在本质上会随着嵌套层级的加深而增加调用栈深度。
相反，Deser 颠倒了这一流程：由数据格式告诉类型下一个值是什么，并将事件推送到接收槽（sink）中。当一个 sink 遇到嵌套值的起始时，它不会直接调用进入，而是将一个新的 sink 交还给驱动器（driver），驱动器将所有状态保存在堆上（实际上是在一个 arena 内存池中）。在退出时，发射器（emitter）会返回它们的嵌套值，而不是通过递归进入它们。
这也意味着 Deser 无法支持像 protobuf 这样非自描述的数据格式。事实上，它们是完全被刻意排除在设计之外的。换句话说：如果你想“修复”Serde，就必须做出其他妥协。
Deser 大多数想法的起因都可以追溯到 Sentry Relay，它需要处理海量的不可信 JSON。在 Sentry 的那些年里，我们反复遇到同一套问题，其中许多其实并不是 Serde 的 bug，而是其设计的必然结果。Serde 的稳定性保证意味着很多问题在不破坏现有格式和手写实现的前提下是无法修复的。这些问题大多源于以下三个决策：
所有格式共用一套 trait。Serde 既服务于自描述格式（JSON、YAML、TOML 等），也服务于读取方必须预先知道类型的格式（postcard、bincode、protobuf 等）。这极其有用，但也意味着某些特性仅对部分格式有效，并且你只能在运行时才发现。在 Serde 中，这也导致了一些奇怪的瑕疵，例如派生出的结构体在 JSON 中会静默接受一个数组来代替对象。
固定且在缓冲时会丢失信息的数据模型。内部带标签的枚举、无标签枚举以及 flatten 在知道如何处理值之前，都需要对值进行缓冲。缓冲区无法保留该格式原本已知的所有信息，错误会丢失其具体位置，生态系统的扩展则不得不依赖带内信令来表达任意精度数字等内容。
调用栈上的递归。每一层嵌套都会消耗栈空间。各种格式通过设置递归深度上限来防御此类问题，但一旦走到了没有深度限制的代码路径（如写入、动态值），深层嵌套的数据就可能使你的进程崩溃。这也意味着在等待更多输入时，反序列化过程是无法暂停的。
许多对应的 Serde issue 已经开启了数年之久，我之前也写过关于滥用 Serde 的文章。多年来，人们尝试从不同角度来解决这个问题。有些人走向极简路线，去掉了绝大多数特性以换取极快的编译速度和零递归。dtolnay 自己的 miniserde 就是最好的例子，deser 最初的 trait 设计正是以此为原型的。其他最近的尝试则走向了运行时反射，或是专注于二进制格式的新数据模型。
如果你想全面了解汇总起来的 Serde 设计挑战，我在这个链接维护了一份长长的清单。
首先，我认为替换掉 Serde 是不太可能的。孤儿规则（orphan rule）使 Serde 在生态系统中根深蒂固。但有些事情是 crate 作者力所能及的。对于 Deser 而言，那就是完整性。
今天的 Deser 实现了所有重要的自描述格式，包括 YAML、JSON、TOML、CBOR、JSON5 等，同时也支持 XML 和 plist 以真正填补空白。尤其是 XML，这是 Serde 明确拒绝支持的格式，其劣势显而易见（下文详述）。至少，格式支持不应该成为拒绝使用 Deser 的理由。
第二个常见问题是，真正解决 Serde 的问题往往需要在编译时间和/或运行时性能上付出巨大代价。Deser 也不例外。虽然 Deser 的编译时间比 Serde 略好，但二进制文件体积膨胀却严重得多，运行时性能也是互有胜负。从数据上看整体相当，但取决于数据格式的结构，某些权衡取舍会带来明显的性能损失。
即便如此，它现在所处的状态，至少在原则上已经可以作为一个直接替代品（drop-in replacement），其中的取舍对于某些用户来说可能恰到好处。
在表层使用上，Deser 并未试图与 Serde 表现出太大的差异。在大多数场景下，你只需 derive Serialize 和 Deserialize，然后配合你选择的格式实现 crate 开始使用。大多数属性（attributes）都非常相似，不过它们接受的是 Rust 表达式而不是字符串。

如果你亲自实现一个序列化器或反序列化器，这种设计上的差异就会变得更加明显。它不再采用相互递归调用的访问者（visitor），反序列化某个类型时会创建一个接收槽（sink），用于接收由解析器直接触发的事件；而序列化则生成分发值的发射器（emitter）。嵌套的接收槽与发射器会被交还给驱动程序（driver），并由其保存在堆上。这种完全借鉴自 miniserde 的设计带来了一些有趣的结果：

除此之外，还有许多我个人一直想要拥有的功能：

以下是一个小型配置类型，同时展示了其中的几项特性：

适配器本身就是类型，因此 Hex 可以放在 Vec 内部，DisplayFromStr 也可以放在 Option 内部的 Vec 内部。验证器同样也是适配器，因此 Check > 会先对键进行解码，然后检查是否至少包含一个键。而兜底（catch-all）变体则保留了标签以及其余所有内容的记录，以备日后有人需要进行处理。

错误处理是我非常重视的部分，以下展示了当某个值出现错误时发生的情况：

请注意，这里的内部标记枚举（internally tagged enum）的标签位于最后，这意味着在确定标签之前必须先对这些值进行缓冲。在 Serde 中这非常棘手，如果我们采用某些技巧来添加定位，往往会丢失位置信息。然而在 Deser 中，一旦启用了路径层（path layer），Deser 便能指出问题出现在数据结构的哪个具体位置：

Deser 非常注重可扩展性，而 XML 则是体现 Deser 与 Serde 之间差异的一个更极端的例子。以下是一个混入了用于作者信息的 Dublin Core 的 Atom 条目：

XML 使用命名空间，这意味着名称需要通过其命名空间来进行匹配，而不是依赖文档碰巧使用的前缀。在此处，文档中使用的是 d:，而类型定义中声明的是 dc!。atom!("title") 实际上就是字符串 {http://www.w3.org/2005/Atom}title，之所以能这样运作是因为属性支持表达式。尽管两个 creator 之间隔着另一个元素，它们仍然会被收集到同一个 Vec 中，而 updated 的文本则直接解析为 chrono 日期时间。由于该枚举是未标记的（untagged），该条目在选定变体之前必须进行缓冲，而 deser 的缓冲区同时保留了两个 creator。因此最终结果是一个同时包含 John 和 Jane 的 Entry。

quick-xml 作为 Serde 最流行的 XML crate，会丢弃前缀并完全忽略命名空间，因此来自其他命名空间的 也会被欣然接受为该条目的标题。然而，分散列表（split list）的处理情况则要糟糕得多。一个普通的 Entry 会因为 creator 字段重复而报错失败，除非你开启 overlapped-lists 特性（请记住，这是一个全局累加标志，任何 crate 都可以设置）。该特性使 quick-xml 预读到元素的末尾并缓冲中间的所有内容，除非你手动设置限制，否则没有上限。

但是该特性仅在 quick-xml 直接对接结构体且没有发生额外缓冲时才有效。如果将该结构体包裹在未标记枚举中，Serde 就会自行对该条目进行缓冲。从该缓冲区读取时，Entry 再次遇到了两次 creator 并重新报错。其回退方案是使用 map，但 map 仅保留最后一个 creator，且不会报错。无论开启还是关闭该特性，你都会得到如下结果：

请注意，John 已经丢失了。

特定格式的扩展类型（例如 TOML 日期时间）是另一个典型案例。TOML 原生支持它们，但 Serde 的数据模型不支持，因此 toml crate 会将它们作为带有一个特殊魔术键的 map 传递下去。而在 Deser 中，日期时间属于扩展值，能识别它的格式会予以保留，而所有其他格式则将其写入为字符串：

同样的情况若在 serde_json::Value 下，你会得到 {"released":{"$__toml_private_datetime":"2026-09-29T21:00:00+02:00"}}，并且将该值直接读取到 chrono::DateTime 中会彻底失败，报错为无效类型：map，预期为 RFC 3339 格式的日期和时间字符串。

既然你已经了解到 Deser 至少在理论上非常出色，那么它的代价是什么呢？

天下没有免费的午餐。该设计依赖于动态分发以及保存在堆上的接收槽和发射器，这带来了可观的运行时开销。在我自己对 JSON 的基准测试中，取决于具体数据，Deser 的读取速度在比 serde_json 快 33% 到慢 60% 之间波动。平均而言，读取速度慢大约 10%。写入速度在快 3 倍到慢 70% 之间，平均下来基本持平。对于 YAML 和 TOML，它明显快于基于 Serde 的 crate，但这更多归功于格式的具体实现而非整体架构。

编译时间略有改善，但并不显著。由于它没有对所有内容进行单态化（monomorphize），派生代码的 release 构建速度大约是 Serde 的 2.3 倍，并且在实践中对于你自己的代码还会更好一点，因为所需的重新编译更少。

为了让 Deser 的设计完全行得通，它在内部也使用了 unsafe。其中大部分是为了在堆上维护借用的接收槽链。我觉得在当今拥有 Miri 和各类工具/智能体的时代，这完全没有问题，但我知道这会让某些人感到不安。

而且，最大的代价在于它终究不是 Serde。

实际上支持的功能相当多，这可能会让人感到惊讶。除了核心功能外，还提供了对 derive 的支持。

它支持你能想到的所有 JSON 变体：JSON、JSONC、JSON5 和 HJSON。（这里有个有趣的事实：它们都是从同一个共享解析器模板生成的）。对于二进制处理，它支持 CBOR 和 MessagePack。此外，它还支持 YAML 1.1 和 1.2、TOML、XML 以及苹果 plist 的全部三种格式，外加 CSV/TSV、urlencoded 数据和环境变量。对于更高级的复杂需求，你可以附加路径信息或捕获位置数据，同时也支持调试打印。你可以在解析的同时执行验证，除 base64 之外还能自由选用不同的二进制编码，你可以桥接到 serde 或捕获动态值，在不同格式之间进行代码转码，或者将其与 tokio 集成。

如需阅读文档，请参阅 docs.rs/deser，源代码连同许多示例均已托管在 GitHub 上。

trendStories.fullContent:
Though not yet approved by any regulatory agency, retatrutide could help improve blood sugar levels and reduce inflammation

The ‘Godzilla’ of weight-loss drugs could help improve blood sugar levels, reduce inflammation and cut a person’s body weight by a quarter, according to the largest study of its kind.

Retatrutide mimics three key gut hormones that help control appetite, blood sugar and metabolism: GLP-1, GIP and glucagon. Unlike other drugs such as Wegovy, which primarily targets the GLP-1 pathway to suppress appetite, or Mounjaro, which contains GLP-1 plus GIP to control blood sugar levels, retatrutide also engages the glucagon receptor, which helps increase energy expenditure.
trendStories.fullTranslation:
尽管尚未获得任何监管机构的批准，但瑞他鲁肽（retatrutide）或有助于改善血糖水平并减轻炎症。

同类研究中规模最大的一项研究显示，这款被誉为减重药物界“哥斯拉”的药物，或可帮助改善血糖水平、减轻炎症，并使人的体重减轻四分之一。

瑞他鲁肽模拟了三种有助于控制食欲、血糖和新陈代谢的关键肠道激素：GLP-1、GIP 和胰高血糖素（glucagon）。与其他药物不同——例如主要通过靶向 GLP-1 通路来抑制食欲的 Wegovy，或是结合 GLP-1 和 GIP 来控制血糖水平的 Mounjaro——瑞他鲁肽还能激活胰高血糖素受体，从而有助于增加能量消耗。

trendStories.title: 两种不同类型的 SQL 查询构造器
trendStories.originalTitle: Two Kinds of SQL Query Builders
trendStories.fullContent:
The SQL language has a paradoxical fate. Although it was deliberately designed to appeal to a human user, nowadays most of SQL code is written—or rather generated—by the computer. Many computer programs need to query some database, and, for the vast majority of database servers, the only supported query language is SQL. But generating SQL is difficult because of the complicated and obscure rules of its quasi-English grammar (its original name SEQUEL stands for Structured English Query Language). For this reason, programs that interact with a database often use specialized libraries for generating SQL queries.

One of such libraries is FunSQL. FunSQL is designed with two goals in mind: supporting the full range of SQL's querying capabilities and exposing these capabilities in a compositional, data-oriented interface. This combination of goals makes FunSQL a perfect tool for data analysis in SQL and differentiates it from all the other query building libraries. Many query builders offer good coverage of SQL features, fewer provide data-oriented interface, but only FunSQL combines them in a single package.

And yet the difference between FunSQL and other query builders is not immediately apparent. In fact, the interfaces of various query building libraries seem almost identical. A query that finds 100 oldest male patients (in the OMOP CDM database) is assembled with FunSQL as follows:

The same query can be written in Ruby using Active Record Query Interface:

Or in PHP with Laravel's Query Builder:

Or in R with dbplyr:

In each of these code samples, the query is assembled using essentially the same interface. Stripped of its syntactic shell, the process of assembling the query can be visualized as a diagram of five processing nodes connected in a pipeline:

It is precisely the fact that the query is progressively assembled using atomic, independent components that lets us call this interface compositional.

However we did claim that FunSQL differs from all the other query building libraries, and now apparently proved the opposite? As a matter of fact, there is a difference, even if it is not reflected in notation. To demonstrate this, let us rearrange this pipeline, moving the Order and the Limit nodes in front of Where.

How does this rearrangement affect the output of the query? Perhaps unexpectedly, the answer depends on the library. With FunSQL, as well as EF/LINQ and dbplyr, it changes the output from 100 oldest male patients to the males among 100 oldest patients. But not so with the other two libraries, Active Record and Laravel, where rearranging the pipeline has no effect on the output.

To summarize, the following query builders are sensitive to the order of the pipeline nodes:

And the following are not:

These are the two kinds of query builders from this article's title. But how can these libraries act so differently while sharing the same interface? To answer this question, we need to focus on what is only implicitly present on the pipeline diagram: the information that is processed by the pipeline nodes.

A node with one incoming and one outgoing arrow symbolizes a processing unit that takes the input data, transforms it, and emits the output data. While the character of the data is not revealed, it is tempting to assume it to be the tabular data extracted from the database.

But this can't be right, at least not literally, because a SQL query builder cannot read the data in the database. Instead, the query builder generates a SQL query:

But if we assume for a moment that pipeline nodes could process the data directly, we would expect that both the pipeline and the corresponding SQL query produce the same output. In other words, the role of the pipeline is to specify the expected output of the SQL query. This is how pipeline nodes are interpreted by FunSQL and the other two libraries, EF/LINQ and dbplyr. We can call such query builders data-oriented.

The conversion of the pipeline to SQL is not always that straightforward. Even though we could freely reorder the nodes in a pipeline, we cannot do the same to the clauses in a SQL query. This is because the SQL grammar arranges the clauses in a rigid order:

This order is compatible with the first pipeline, in which the Where node is followed by Order and Limit, but not the second pipeline, where these nodes change their relative positions. So how could the second pipeline be converted to SQL? We would be out of options if we were still using the original SQL standard, SQL-86, but the next revision of the language, SQL-92, recognized this limitation. Regrettably, it did not relax this rigid clause order. Instead, SQL-92 introduced a workaround: a query can be extended by nesting it into the next query's FROM clause. This gives us a method for converting an arbitrary pipeline into SQL: break the pipeline into smaller chunks that comply with the SQL clause order, convert each chunk into a SQL query, and then nest all these queries together:

The SQL grammar has a number of deficiencies, including rigid clause order, query nesting, and nonsensical position of the SELECT clause. The position of SELECT violates the execution flow of the query, and this violation is aggravated by query nesting. Complex SQL queries often require multiple levels of nesting, which makes such queries bloated and difficult to interpret. This is where data-oriented query builders, which do not constrain the order of pipeline nodes, offer an improvement over plain SQL.

What about the other kind of query builders? Active Record and Laravel employ a pipeline of exactly the same form, but because it is not sensitive to the order of the nodes, it must work on a different principle. Indeed, this pipeline generates a SQL query by incrementally assembling the SQL syntax tree. Because of the rigid clause order, a SQL syntax tree can be faithfully represented as a composite data structure with slots specifying the content of the SELECT, FROM, WHERE, and the other clauses:

Individual slots of this structure are populated by the corresponding pipeline nodes.

This explains why the pipeline is insensitive to the order of the nodes. Indeed, as long as the content of the slots stays the same, it makes no difference in what order the slots are populated.

This method of incrementally constructing a composite structure is known as the builder pattern. We can call the query builders that employ this pattern syntax-oriented.

Both data-oriented and syntax-oriented query builders are compositional: the difference is in the nature of the information processed by the units of composition. Data-oriented query builders incrementally refine the query output; syntax-oriented query builders incrementally assemble the SQL syntax tree. Their interfaces look almost identical, but their methods of operation are fundamentally different.

But which one is better? Syntax-oriented query builders have two definite advantages: they are easy to implement and they could support the full range of SQL features. Indeed, the interface of a syntax-oriented query builder is just a collection of builders for the SQL syntax tree. How complete the representation of the syntax tree determines how well various SQL features are supported.

On the other hand, syntax-oriented query builders are harder to use. As they directly represent the SQL grammar, they inherit all of its deficiencies. In particular, the rigid clause order makes it difficult to assemble complex data processing pipelines, especially when the arrangement of pipeline nodes is not predetermined.

A data-oriented query builder directly represents data processing nodes, which makes assembling data processing pipelines much more straightforward—as long as we can find the necessary nodes among those offered by the builder. But where does the builder get its collection of data processing nodes? And how can we tell if this collection is complete?

One way to implement a data-oriented query builder is to adapt a general-purpose query framework. Indeed, this is the origin of EF/LINQ, which is adapted from LINQ, and dbplyr, which is adapted from dplyr. The query framework determines what processing nodes are available and how they operate. In principle, any query framework could be adapted to SQL databases by introducing just one new node, a node that loads the content of a database table. If we place this node at the beginning of a pipeline and make the rest of it out of regular nodes, we obtain a pipeline that processes data from a SQL database. However, this pipeline will be very inefficient compared to a SQL engine, which can use indexes to avoid loading the entire table into memory and thus can process the same data much faster. This is why EF/LINQ and dbplyr generate a SQL query that replaces the pipeline as a whole. The pipeline itself no longer runs directly, but now serves as a specification, with the assumption that if it were to run, it would produce the same output as the SQL query. This method of transforming a general-purpose query framework to a SQL query builder is called SQL pushdown.

However, SQL pushdown has a serious limitation. A general-purpose query framework is not designed with SQL compatibility in mind. For this reason, some of the pipelines assembled within this framework cannot be converted to SQL. Even worse, many useful SQL queries have no equivalent pipelines and thus cannot be generated using SQL pushdown. Indeed, SQL accumulated a wide range of features and capabilities since it first appeared in 1974. The first revision of the SQL standard, SQL-86, already supported Cartesian products, filtering, grouping, aggregation, and correlated subqueries. The next revision, SQL-92, added many join types and introduced query nesting. SQL:1999 greatly expanded its analytical capabilities by adding two types of queries: recursive queries, for processing hierarchical data, and data cube queries, which generalize histograms, cross-tabulations, roll-ups, drill-downs, and sub-totals. The follow-up revision, SQL:2003, added support for aggregate functions over a running window. Admittedly, SQL is a quintessential enterprise abomination, a hodgepodge of features added to support every imaginable use case, but with inadequate syntax, weird gaps in functionality, and no regards to internal consistency. Nevertheless, the breadth of SQL's capabilities has not been matched by any other query framework, including LINQ or dplyr. So when we generate SQL queries using EF/LINQ or dbplyr, a large subset of these capabilities remains inaccessible.

FunSQL is a data-oriented query builder created specifically to expose full expressive power of SQL. Unlike EF/LINQ and dbplyr, FunSQL was not adapted from an existing query framework, but was carefully designed from scratch to match SQL's capabilities. These capabilities include, for example, support for correlated subqueries and lateral joins (with Bind node), aggregate and window functions (using Group and Partition nodes), as well as recursive queries (with Iterate node). This comprehensive support for SQL capabilities makes FunSQL the only SQL query builder suitable for assembling complex data processing pipelines. Moreover, even though FunSQL pipelines cannot be run directly, every FunSQL node has a well-defined data processing semantics, which means that, in principle, FunSQL could be developed into a full-blown query framework. This potentially opens a path for replacing SQL with an equally powerful, but a more coherent and expressive query language.
trendStories.fullTranslation:
SQL 语言有着耐人寻味的命运。尽管它在设计之初是为了迎合人类用户的直觉，但如今大部分 SQL 代码都是由计算机编写——更准确地说是生成——的。许多计算机程序都需要查询某种数据库，而对于绝大多数数据库服务器而言，唯一支持的查询语言就是 SQL。但生成 SQL 却很困难，因为其类英语语法规则复杂且晦涩（其原名 SEQUEL 代表“结构化英语查询语言”）。出于这个原因，与数据库交互的程序通常会使用专门的库来生成 SQL 查询。

FunSQL 就是这样的一款库。FunSQL 的设计旨在实现两个目标：支持 SQL 查询功能的全部特性，并通过可组合、面向数据（data-oriented）的接口呈现这些功能。这两个目标的结合使 FunSQL 成为在 SQL 中进行数据分析的理想工具，并使其在所有其他查询构造库中脱颖而出。许多查询构造器都提供了对 SQL 特性的良好覆盖，较少能提供面向数据的接口，但唯有 FunSQL 将二者结合在了一个单独的工具包中。

然而，FunSQL 与其他查询构造器之间的差异并不会立即显现。事实上，各种查询构造库的接口看起来几乎完全相同。一个查找（在 OMOP CDM 数据库中）年龄最大的 100 位男性患者的查询，使用 FunSQL 组装如下：

同样的查询可以使用 Ruby 的 Active Record 查询接口编写：

或者在 PHP 中使用 Laravel 的查询构造器编写：

或者在 R 语言中使用 dbplyr 编写：

在这些代码示例中的每一个，查询本质上都是使用相同的接口组装起来的。剥离掉语法外壳后，组装查询的过程可以直观地展示为一个由管道连接的五个处理节点构成的图表：

正是由于查询是使用原子的、独立的组件逐步组装起来的这一事实，才让我们将这种接口称为“可组合的”（compositional）。

然而，我们此前声称 FunSQL 与所有其他查询构造库截然不同，而现在看起来却证明了完全相反的事实？事实上，差异确实存在，即便它没有直接反映在语法记号上。为了证明这一点，让我们重新排列这个管道，将 Order 和 Limit 节点移动到 Where 节点的前面。

这种重新排列对查询的输出有什么影响？出人意料的是，答案取决于具体的库。对于 FunSQL，以及 EF/LINQ 和 dbplyr，这会将输出从“100 位最年长的男性患者”改变为“100 位最年长的患者中的男性”。但对于另外两个库（Active Record 和 Laravel）则并非如此，在它们之中，重新排列管道对输出毫无影响。

总括而言，以下查询构造器对管道节点的顺序是敏感的：

而以下查询构造器则不敏感：

这就是本文标题中所说的“两种不同类型的查询构造器”。但是，这些库在共享相同接口的同时，怎么会有如此截然不同的行为？要回答这个问题，我们需要聚焦于管道图表中仅隐含存在的内容：即管道节点所处理的信息。

一个带有一个输入箭头和一个输出箭头的节点，象征着一个处理单元，它获取输入数据，对其进行转换，并输出数据。虽然数据的具体性质尚未揭晓，但人们很容易假设它就是从数据库中提取的表格数据。

但这不可能是正确的，至少在字面上讲不通，因为 SQL 查询构造器无法读取数据库中的数据。相反，查询构造器生成的是一条 SQL 查询：

但如果我们暂时假设管道节点可以直接处理数据，我们就会期望管道和对应的 SQL 查询产生相同的输出。换言之，管道的作用是指定 SQL 查询的预期输出。这就是 FunSQL 以及另外两个库（EF/LINQ 和 dbplyr）解释管道节点的方式。我们可以将此类查询构造器称为“面向数据”（data-oriented）的构造器。

将管道转换为 SQL 并不总是那么直截了当。尽管我们可以在管道中自由地重新排序节点，但我们不能对 SQL 查询中的子句做同样的事情。这是因为 SQL 语法以刚性固定的顺序排列各个子句：

这种顺序与第一个管道兼容（在该管道中，Where 节点之后是 Order 和 Limit），但与第二个管道不兼容（在第二个管道中，这些节点改变了它们的相对位置）。那么第二个管道该如何转换为 SQL 呢？如果我们仍在使用最初的 SQL 标准 SQL-86，我们将会无计可施；但该语言的下一版本 SQL-92 意识到了这一局限性。遗憾的是，它并未放宽这一刚性的子句顺序。取而代之的是，SQL-92 引入了一种变通方案：可以通过将一个查询嵌套到下一个查询的 FROM 子句中来对其进行扩展。这为我们提供了一种将任意管道转换为 SQL 的方法：将管道拆分成符合 SQL 子句顺序的较小块，将每个块转换为一个 SQL 查询，然后将所有这些查询嵌套在一起：

SQL 语法存在诸多缺陷，包括刚性的子句顺序、查询嵌套以及 SELECT 子句荒谬的位置。SELECT 的位置违背了查询的执行流，而这种违背又因查询嵌套而进一步加剧。复杂的 SQL 查询通常需要多层嵌套，这使得此类查询变得臃肿且难以解读。正是在这一点上，不对管道节点顺序做限制的面向数据查询构造器，相比纯 SQL 带来了改进。

那么另一种查询构造器又是怎样的呢？Active Record 和 Laravel 采用了形式完全相同的管道，但因为它对节点的顺序不敏感，所以它必须基于不同的原理工作。事实上，这种管道是通过递增组装 SQL 语法树来生成 SQL 查询的。由于刚性的子句顺序，SQL 语法树可以被真实地表示为一个复合数据结构，其中包含指定 SELECT、FROM、WHERE 和其他子句内容的插槽（slots）：

该结构的各个插槽由相应的管道节点填充。

这就解释了为什么管道对节点的顺序不敏感。事实上，只要插槽的内容保持相同，以何种顺序填充这些插槽便毫无区别。

这种增量构建复合结构的方法被称为“构造器模式”（builder pattern）。我们可以将采用这种模式的查询构造器称为“面向语法”（syntax-oriented）的构造器。

面向数据和面向语法的查询构造器都是可组合的：二者的差异在于组合单元所处理信息的本质。面向数据的查询构造器逐步细化查询输出；面向语法的查询构造器逐步组装 SQL 语法树。它们的接口看起来几乎一模一样，但其运作原理有着本质的不同。

但是哪一种更好呢？面向语法的查询构建器有两个明显的优势：它们易于实现，并且能够支持全套 SQL 特性。事实上，面向语法的查询构建器的接口只不过是 SQL 语法树构建器的集合。对语法树表达的完整程度，决定了其对各种 SQL 特性的支持好坏。

另一方面，面向语法的查询构建器更难使用。由于它们直接体现 SQL 语法，因而继承了其所有的缺陷。特别是其僵化的子句顺序，使得组装复杂的数据处理流水线变得十分困难，尤其是当流水线节点的排列并非预先确定的时候。

面向数据的查询构建器则直接表示数据处理节点，这使得组装数据处理流水线直观得多——只要我们能在构建器提供的节点中找到所需节点即可。但是，构建器从何处获取其数据处理节点集？我们又如何判断这个集合是否完整呢？

实现面向数据查询构建器的一种方法是改造通用查询框架。事实上，这正是 EF/LINQ（由 LINQ 改编而来）和 dbplyr（由 dplyr 改编而来）的由来。查询框架决定了有哪些可用的处理节点以及它们如何运作。原则上，任何查询框架都可以通过仅引入一个新节点——即加载数据库表内容的节点——来适配 SQL 数据库。如果我们把这个节点放在流水线的开头，并用常规节点构建其余部分，就能得到一个处理来自 SQL 数据库的数据的流水线。然而，与 SQL 引擎相比，这种流水线的效率会非常低，因为 SQL 引擎可以利用索引来避免将整张表加载到内存中，从而以极快的速度处理相同的数据。这就是为什么 EF/LINQ 和 dbplyr 会生成一条 SQL 查询来整体替换该流水线。流水线本身不再直接运行，而是充当一种规范，其假设是：如果它真的运行起来，其产生的输出将与该 SQL 查询相同。这种将通用查询框架转换为 SQL 查询构建器的方法被称为“SQL 下推”（SQL pushdown）。

然而，SQL 下推存在严重的局限性。通用查询框架在设计之初并未考虑与 SQL 的兼容性。因此，在此类框架中组装的部分流水线无法转换为 SQL。更糟糕的是，许多实用的 SQL 查询根本没有等价的流水线，因而无法通过 SQL 下推生成。诚然，自 1974 年首次出现以来，SQL 积累了极其丰富的功能与特性。SQL 标准的第一个修订版 SQL-86 就已经支持笛卡尔积、过滤、分组、聚合以及相关子查询。随后的修订版 SQL-92 增加了多种连接类型并引入了查询嵌套。SQL:1999 通过增加两类查询极大地拓展了其分析能力：用于处理层级数据的递归查询，以及泛化了直方图、交叉制表、上卷、下钻和小计的数据立方体（data cube）查询。随后的修订版 SQL:2003 又增加了对滑动窗口聚合函数的支持。不可否认，SQL 是典型的企业级“怪胎”，为了支持所有能想象到的用例而东拼西凑了大量特性，但语法欠佳、功能上存在古怪的缺失，且毫不顾及内部一致性。尽管如此，SQL 功能的广度是任何其他查询框架（包括 LINQ 或 dplyr）都无法比拟的。因此，当我们使用 EF/LINQ 或 dbplyr 生成 SQL 查询时，很大一部分能力仍然是无法触及的。

FunSQL 是一款专为释放 SQL 全部表达能力而创建的面向数据的查询构建器。与 EF/LINQ 和 dbplyr 不同，FunSQL 并非由现有查询框架改造而来，而是从零开始精心设计以匹配 SQL 的各项能力。例如，这些能力包括对相关子查询和横向连接（lateral join）的支持（通过 Bind 节点）、聚合与窗口函数（使用 Group 和 Partition 节点），以及递归查询（使用 Iterate 节点）。对 SQL 功能的这种全面支持，使得 FunSQL 成为唯一适合组装复杂数据处理流水线的 SQL 查询构建器。此外，尽管 FunSQL 流水线无法直接运行，但每个 FunSQL 节点都具有明确定义的数据处理语义，这意味着原则上 FunSQL 可以发展为一个功能完备的查询框架。这有可能开辟一条道路，用一种同样强大、但更连贯且更具表现力的查询语言来取代 SQL。

trendStories.title: Shell 与电子邮件
trendStories.fullContent:
Is email the best way to work when working with multiple agents at the same time? Each email thread is a session. And it supports group conversations.

See what I built on Github.

With email. you’re not chained to a single company’s app or, even, your laptop. You can do it anywhere and email is the most versatile in poor network conditions, on top of that.

Email already solves the problem for working with people in an asynchronous and distributed way. Large language models get this, like they get the shell.

We like the shell and the terminal that let’s us use it. And for practical reasons. The shell composes and enables interoperability with other applications without a gatekeeper. Once you get the hang of it, using the terminal is fun and liberating.

There is no coincidence that LLMs are most useful to us when harnessed to the shell. And if we need to work very closely with an agent, doing so from the terminal is best so we can be as close to the shell as possible.

I’m thankful for that. We mostly use Claude Code, Codex CLI, and others, such as OpenCode that uses the shell and are worked with by us on the terminal (uses the shell). We don’t have to use an iPhone App or some cloud based web app by a single company to use a computer productively.

However, there are clearly limitations when you must work with many agents. It’s dizzying. We often need to work asynchronously with agents working on different things. Stop. Do something else. Live life. Check on it a bit. Return to it easily on our own time, etc.

Again, email already solves the problem for working with people in an asynchronous and distributed way. That translates well when working with agents, and even other people and agents.

After the first release of Machtiani over a year ago, I began feeding Machtiani’s answers back into its next instructions. I didn’t release until now to pursue this. An iterative instructions loop that drove a worker that is lightweight supervisor.

That lightweight supervisor can work with any agents already installed on your computer.

I found email be the most natural and liberating way to work with others and agents together.

See Machtiani on GitHub.
trendStories.fullTranslation:
当同时与多个智能体（Agent）协作时，电子邮件是最佳的工作方式吗？每一个邮件主题线（thread）就是一个会话，而且它天生支持群组对话。

在 GitHub 上看看我构建的项目。

借助电子邮件，你不会被束缚在某家公司的单一应用中，甚至不必拘泥于你的笔记本电脑。你可以在任何地方操作，此外，电子邮件在恶劣的网络环境下也是适应性最强的。

电子邮件已经解决了以异步和分布式方式与人协作的问题。大语言模型懂得这一点，就像它们懂得 Shell 一样。

我们喜欢 Shell 以及让我们得以使用它的终端。这背后有着非常务实的原因：Shell 能够进行组合，并在无需任何守门人把控的情况下与其他应用程序实现互操作。一旦你掌握了门道，使用终端就会变得既有趣又让人感到自由。

当大语言模型与 Shell 结合时能发挥最大效用，这绝非巧合。如果我们必须与某个智能体紧密协作，在终端中进行是最好的选择，这样我们就能尽可能贴近 Shell。

我对此深怀感激。我们主要使用 Claude Code、Codex CLI 以及其他工具（例如使用 Shell 的 OpenCode），并通过终端与它们协同工作（使用 Shell）。我们不必为了高效使用计算机而被迫去用 iPhone 应用或某家公司基于云的 Web 应用。

然而，当你必须同时与多个智能体协作时，局限性就显而易见了。那种体验令人眼花缭乱。我们往往需要以异步方式与负责不同任务的智能体协同工作：停下来，去做别的事情，过好日常生活，抽空查看一下进度，在我们自己的时间节奏里轻松返回任务等等。

再说一次，电子邮件已经解决了以异步和分布式方式与人协作的问题。这种模式非常自然地延伸到了与智能体协作、乃至人与智能体混合协作的场景中。

在一年多前首次发布 Machtiani 之后，我开始将 Machtiani 的回答重新喂回给它的下一轮指令中。为了探索这一方向，我直到现在才发布新版本：一个驱动着工作者的迭代指令循环，而这个工作者正是一个轻量级的监督者（supervisor）。

这个轻量级监督者可以与你计算机上已安装的任何智能体协同工作。

我发现，电子邮件是与他人以及智能体共同协作最自然、最让人感到自由的方式。

欢迎在 GitHub 上查看 Machtiani。

ticker.snippet: 【中新网 (全球要闻原版)·独立专业观察】：中新网9月30日电 据“市说新语”微信公众号消息，市场监管总局发布的JJF 2385—2026《智能眼镜声学性能测试规范》国家计量技术规范(以下简称《规范》)将自10月2日起正式实施，为智能眼镜声学性能检测划定统一技术标尺，以计量法治监管守护消费权益，助力新兴消费品行业高质量发展。
